            available_excerpt: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized
              and encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
              state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
              state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or
              \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner]
              is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
              to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through
              the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue
              a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication to acquire
              control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny the application.
              The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific
              reasons for the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
              is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal
              within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the
              denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
              requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the
              \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose
              of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the shareholders or holders of
              voting shares or voting interests of a \nlicensee or a person in control
              of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
              by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
              as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator, or
              trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction
              or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section
              3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not
              subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA
              public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control of
              \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in control
              of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the licensee
              remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4),
              (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
              within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary:
              Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision may
              be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act
              should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
              Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

            available_excerpt: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1)
              \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
              that has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission
              \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior
              application filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an
              MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided
              that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended
              or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended
              while the person \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years;
              \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the person is well managed and
              \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its
              most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if such rating
              was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to meet
              the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]
              after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person acquiring
              control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the
              requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after
              the acquisition of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be
              acquired will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan
              as a result of the acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring
              control is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material
              \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control;
              \ and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation
              \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C),
              and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner].
              \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date
              on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed
              approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire
              control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination
              from the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered
              a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction.
              If the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person
              in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction is not
              subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act].
              \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes a determination pursuant
              to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise
              subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
              is authorized and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of
              a lead investigative state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and
              \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

                - start: 0
                  end: 3962
                  text: '# Known Facts


                    - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                    (~10 weeks out).

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                    - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                    by Harbor.

                    - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                    four new markets.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                    has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                    - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                    transfer, launching close+1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance.

                    - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                    users were already KYC''d.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                    feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                    - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                    (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                    - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                    on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                    - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                    the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                    Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                    - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                    identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                    known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                    on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                    - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                    year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                    and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                    what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                    to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                    ## Assumptions


                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                    and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                    the acquisition without new state approval

                    - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                    Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                    documents

                    - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                    and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                    - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                    to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                    confirmed).

                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                    in 41 states (per the request).

                    - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                    purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                    obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                    '
                source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                  text: '# Issues and workstreams


                    - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                    under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                    transfer/survive the acquisition

                    - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                    missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                    Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                    - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                    Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                    - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                    when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                    - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                    money transmission or consumer protection implications

                    - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                    -->

                    '

                    population and can create immediate exposure that is difficult

                  text: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
                    or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                    certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant
                    that is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner].
                    If the certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner]
                    may order the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner]
                    may find necessary to enable the independent or certified public
                    accountant or \nindependent public accountant to remove the qualification.
                    \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee
                    shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45 days \nof
                    the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized
                    and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report
                    required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
                    is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b)
                    \nThe authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum,
                    each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2)
                    \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider
                    identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address;
                    \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious
                    or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number, and
                    email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10)
                    \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;
                    \ \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12)
                    \nAny other information the [Commissioner] reasonably requires
                    with \nrespect to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports
                    of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed
                    to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting
                    \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize
                    NMLS to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops
                    new functionality to prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"

                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md
                  text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
                    within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know
                    of the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe
                    filing of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited
                    States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended
                    or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization;
                    \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee for
                    \nreceivership, the commencement of any other judicial or administrative
                    proceeding for its \ndissolution or reorganization, or the making
                    of a general assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or
                    \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend
                    its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee engages
                    in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report
                    with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
                    licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
                    events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of
                    a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a
                    felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate
                    for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee
                    and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required by
                    federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity
                    reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act
                    and other federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering.
                    The timely filing of \na complete and accurate report required
                    under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency
                    is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section 7.05].
                    \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
                    records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for
                    at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money
                    transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted
                    at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income,
                    and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
                    records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"

                    [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained in any form of \nrecord. \n(c)
                    \nRecords specified in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained outside
                    this state \nif they are made accessible to the [Commissioner]
                    on [seven] business-days' notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d)
                    \nAll records maintained by the licensee as required in [Section
                    7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to inspection by the [Commissioner] pursuant
                    to [Section 4.03(a)]. \n \nARTICLE VIII \nAuthorized Delegates
                    \nSection 8.01 Relationship Between Licensee and Authorized Delegate.
                    \n(a) \nIn this [Section 8.01], \"remit\" means to make direct
                    payments of money to \na licensee or its representative authorized
                    to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in an \naccount
                    specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee is authorized
                    to conduct business through an authorized \ndelegate or allows
                    a person to act as the licensee's authorized delegate, the licensee
                    must: \n(1) \nadopt, and update as necessary, written policies
                    and procedures \nreasonably designed to ensure that the licensee's
                    authorized delegates comply with \napplicable state and federal
                    law; \n(2) \nenter into a written contract that complies with
                    [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct a reasonable risk-based
                    background investigation sufficient \nfor the licensee to determine
                    whether the authorized delegate has complied and will likely \ncomply
                    with applicable state and federal law. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate
                    must operate in full compliance with this [Act]. \n(d) \nThe written
                    contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed by the \nlicensee
                    and the authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"

                    but not limited to, prices and fees for such bond is \nredacted;
                    \n(5) \nCopies of any non-confidential final orders of the [Department]
                    \nrelating to any violation of this [Act] or regulations implementing
                    this [Act]; and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or
                    penalty under this [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe
                    [Commissioner] may conduct an examination or investigation of
                    a \nlicensee or authorized delegate or otherwise take independent
                    action authorized by this [Act] or by \na rule adopted or order
                    issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary or appropriate
                    to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing
                    this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy
                    Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may: \n(1) \nconduct
                    an examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner]
                    may reasonably require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction
                    with an examination \nconducted by representatives of other state
                    agencies or agencies of another state or of the \nfederal government;
                    \n(3) \n  accept the examination report of another state agency
                    or an agency \nof another state or of the federal government,
                    or a report prepared by an independent \naccounting firm, which
                    on being accepted is considered for all purposes as an official
                    report \nof the [Commissioner]; and \n(4) \nsummon and examine
                    under oath a key individual or employee of a \nlicensee or authorized
                    delegate and require the person to produce records regarding any
                    \nmatter related to the condition and business of the licensee
                    or authorized delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized delegate
                    shall provide, and the [Commissioner] \nshall have full and complete
                    access to, all records the [Commissioner] may reasonably require
                    to \nconduct a complete examination. The records must be provided
                    at the location and in the format \nspecified by the [Commissioner],
                    provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize multistate record \nproduction
                    standards and examination procedures when such standards will
                    reasonably achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8
                    \n(c) \nUnless otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee
                    shall pay all \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an
                    examination of the licensee or the licensee's \n \n8 Commentary:
                    The [Commissioner] is encouraged to instruct examiners to: (1)
                    include all examination requests in \nthe Day 1 letter that may
                    require the licensee to obtain records located outside of the
                    U.S., including but not limited \nto evidence demonstrating when
                    an outstanding money transmission obligation has been extinguished;
                    and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as provided to the
                    licensee by the bank.\n"

          - source_id: SRC-LOCAL-df5dd9f25cf0547e2d1e
            source_hash: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
            source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
            path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-df5dd9f25cf0547e2d1e.md

            title: SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
            support_state: supplied
            source_type: workspace
            available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


              - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
              out).

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

              - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

              - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
              Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

              - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.

              - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay''s engine on day 1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

              - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor''s assets)

              - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
              institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

              - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
              Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for
              its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

              - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
              is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.

              - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


              ## Assumptions


              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
              and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
              acquisition without new state approval

              - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

              - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap

              - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to
              state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).

              - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).

              '

            source_type: workspace
            available_excerpt: '# Issues and workstreams


              - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
              the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
              the acquisition

              - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
              underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
              CIP/AML obligations

              - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

              - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
              when the SaaS contract terminates at close

              - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state money
              transmission or consumer protection implications

              - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
              -->

              '

            available_excerpt: "# Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring

              priorities (private matter context):\nMake KYC, alert resolution, and

            available_excerpt: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall

              to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary to enable
              the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent public
              accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate
              Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized
              delegates within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The
              [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the
              submission of the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided
              that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the requirements of this
              [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall include,
              at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany legal name;
              \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider
              identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6)
              \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or
              trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number, and email \n(9)
              \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting
              as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court orders
              pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information the
              [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect to the authorized
              delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary:
              This language is designed to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform
              Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States
              are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting requirements
              if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize reporting of significant
              events.\n"

            available_excerpt: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with

              \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited
              States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified
              from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing
              of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement
              of any other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution
              or reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit
              of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke
              or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee
              engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a
              report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
              licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
              events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key
              individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2)
              \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
              \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
              delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
              record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set
              forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining
              to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
              report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal
              \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section
              7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
              records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least
              [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least monthly
              containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income, and expense accounts;
              \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords
              of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"

              questions:
              - question_id: Q-SAR
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
                consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item;
                  they can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close
                  and could affect the deal itself.
                state: answered
                answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and
                  remain in diligence.
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids:
                - FACT-20260909-070aec
              - question_id: Q-KYC
                text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations?
                consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
                  gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
                  obligations for these users.
                state: answered
                answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program
                  permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids:
                - FACT-20260909-620c62
              - question_id: Q-MTL
                text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers?
                consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
                  on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating
                  regulatory question.
                state: answered
                answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
                  for the four new markets.
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids:
                - FACT-20260909-771ee1
              - question_id: Q-BONUS
                text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
                consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
                  disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
                state: left_open

                passages: &id112
                - start: 0
                  end: 1441
                  text: '# Issues and workstreams


                    - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                    under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                    transfer/survive the acquisition

                    - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                    missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                    Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                    - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                    Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                    - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                    when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                    - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                    money transmission or consumer protection implications

                    - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                    -->

                    - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
                    <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

                    - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase
                    <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->

                    - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
                    -->

                    - Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
                    -->

                    - Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
                    -->

                    - Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
                    issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->

                    '
                source_version: 916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac

                passages: &id113
                - start: 0
                  end: 3962
                  text: '# Known Facts


                    - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                    (~10 weeks out).

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                    - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                    by Harbor.

                    - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                    four new markets.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                    has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                    - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                    transfer, launching close+1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance.

                    - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                    users were already KYC''d.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                    feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                    - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                    (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                    - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                    on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                    - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                    the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                    Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                    - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                    identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                    known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                    on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                    - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                    year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                    and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                    what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                    to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                    ## Assumptions


                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                    and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                    the acquisition without new state approval

                    - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                    Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                    documents

                    - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                    and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                    - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                    to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                    confirmed).

                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                    in 41 states (per the request).

                    - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                    purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                    obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                    '

                  text: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter dossier)


                    Matter MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated
                    Sep 9–10, 2026. Business question supplied by the matter record;
                    direction unchanged.


                    ## Current position


                    Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review
                    before the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before
                    the deal terms are settled, not merely before launch. This is
                    not "just a data migration": the day-1 plan depends on results
                    the records show are unconfirmed — license coverage in the added
                    markets, the ability to rely on Harbor''s KYC without the underlying
                    records, and a monitoring cutover with no gap.


                    Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


                    - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day
                    1.** The plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established
                    for an asset purchase. If approvals are missing, those markets
                    are a post-close target, not day-1 access. (The number of added
                    states is itself unresolved — see Record conflicts.)


                    - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit
                    reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort
                    with missing documents can keep full access without re-verification
                    or limits.


                    - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether
                    monitoring transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the
                    most decision-changing item because it can affect deal protections
                    and how affected customers are handled at migration.


                    The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms
                    side of the data move do not block close on today''s record, but
                    each must be reviewed before its own go-live point and each needs
                    documents not in the readable record.


                    What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance
                    data pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review
                    protocol for the alerts/SARs. What should wait or change: launching
                    the added markets on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding
                    of users whose verification cannot be evidenced; the monitoring
                    cutover unless a tested no-gap design or a bridge exists; the
                    bonus until its terms are reviewed.


                    This draft recommends treating those items as pre-close gates
                    and preparing a staged launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s
                    recommendation, not a recorded decision. The recorded plan is
                    unchanged: day-1 full migration, no re-verification, use/assume
                    Harbor''s licenses, bonus at close+1. The only recorded lawyer
                    decisions are the Sep 9 intake answers (asset purchase; compliance
                    to confirm KYC reliance; alerts/SARs unreviewed; use/assume Harbor''s
                    licenses). A complete dossier rewrite was submitted as a tracked
                    revision on Sep 10 and, per the record, left the current dossier
                    unchanged pending acceptance; generating this draft records no
                    new decision.


                    ## Decision question


                    Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
                    review before the Nov 15 close?


                    ## Issues


                    The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the
                    Sep 9 initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the
                    lawyer''s "four issues" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]):
                    licensing, KYC/AML, alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The
                    saved issue list and its ISS identifiers were not inside this
                    run''s readable material, so no issue IDs or markers are asserted
                    here. A fifth issue, newly identified in this draft from the recorded
                    migration plan, is included and labeled.


                    Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the
                    readable records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research
                    with sources ([source:MSG-20260909-660683], [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]),
                    an initial "research is in progress" statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d])
                    later corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec], [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]),
                    and a run described as "queued or running" with saved source choices
                    ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output was readable here.
                    Every legal proposition below is therefore a framework or lead,
                    not verified support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**.
                    Each issue gets an initial answer; any prior researched issue
                    answers in the nine captured documents were not readable in this
                    run and should be merged when available.


                    ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


                    **Current answer**


                    Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically
                    carry Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate
                    legal entity cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses.
                    Until a state-by-state path exists — new license, transfer or
                    change-of-control approval in the transaction, or an arrangement
                    where the licensed entity performs the transmission — the added
                    markets should be treated as post-close, not part of day-1 full
                    access. Even where Mosaic holds its own license, the account migration
                    may trigger state notices or filings (unverified).


                    **Rule and support**


                    State money transmitter statutes generally require a license,
                    or status as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit
                    money for others; licenses are issued to a specific entity, and
                    state approval is commonly required for a change of control or
                    transfer of a licensed business [**Needs checking** — the MTL
                    statutes of the specific states; the CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
                    Act where adopted]. Federal MSB registration (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380)
                    is a separate requirement and does not substitute for state licensure
                    [**Needs checking**]. The precise research question: for each
                    state where Mosaic lacks a license and Harbor holds one, what
                    route lets Mosaic lawfully serve migrated customers — new license,
                    license transfer, change-of-control approval, or authorized-delegate
                    arrangement — on what timeline, and what customer or regulator
                    notices accompany the change?


                    **Application**


                    Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
                    Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
                    licenses"; full acce'

                - start: 0
                  end: 5937
                  text: '## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close targeted Nov 15)


                    **Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition
                    migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close? The newest
                    turn ("Generate the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds
                    comparisons are supporting work; they do not change that question.
                    The record contains **no recorded decisions** at all, all five
                    registered issues are `open`, and one intake question — how the
                    $50 bonus is structured — was left open with no answer.


                    **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data
                    migration." The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated
                    event: on day 1 Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its
                    own licensed product set with no re-verification, repoints monitoring,
                    and launches a cash offer — under an asset-purchase structure
                    in which nothing about Harbor''s licenses or compliance record
                    transfers by default. The operative question is therefore not
                    "can we inherit Harbor''s status," but **"what must Mosaic obtain,
                    file, decide or preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which
                    parts of the stated deal upside are not actually available at
                    close."**


                    **Three premises the record lets us test**


                    1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the
                    moment CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach
                    to 252k accounts.

                    2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails
                    on the arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a
                    44-state union yields **three** new states, not four, and the
                    states are never named; and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s
                    licenses rests on an assumption the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]),
                    against the saved position that transferability should not be
                    relied on without a state rule, approval or written regulator
                    position.

                    3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved.
                    Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown,
                    and the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down
                    in 2024; only pass/fail survives).


                    **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9
                    weeks as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read
                    and preserve the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort
                    and schedule remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states;
                    validate the monitoring cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent,
                    new customer terms and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate
                    only in the overlapping states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient
                    accounts with limits — a scoped migration rather than the full
                    one.


                    **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing
                    (44-state footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users;
                    SAR and alert handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring
                    vendor transition at close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are
                    missing and material: **migration data handling and customer notice**
                    (the piece the request actually calls "just a data migration,"
                    never analyzed); **pre-close papering** (closing conditions, interim
                    operation, allocation of the alert/SAR and KYC-record risk — no
                    draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close access to Harbor''s
                    alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS system whose
                    contract ends at close).


                    **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business
                    question, time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


                    1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else
                    is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the deal itself;
                    it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a filing
                    is late or an account must be excluded; and the records needed
                    to answer it may become inaccessible at close.

                    2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify,
                    or restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification"
                    is available at all for the largest population; the underlying
                    documents cannot be recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a
                    cohort is a multi-week program that has to be decided before close,
                    not after.

                    3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull
                    them from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being
                    sold on, state timelines are the longest external dependency and
                    cannot be compressed, and serving a state without authority is
                    a violation later paperwork cannot undo.


                    **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
                    KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the
                    licensing position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
                    — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go
                    decision, licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow
                    the backlog read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market
                    access.


                    **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
                    and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path,
                    and some prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions
                    are not findings about this acquisition. The licensing research
                    has **no citable support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read;
                    one output headed "No external authority retrieved"), and repeated
                    "research queued/running" messages are status, not results. Assumption
                    [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b] still calls the structure unconfirmed
                    although the asset purchase is recorded and was reconfirmed twice
                    by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field (2026-09-11) sits
                    oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat it as unverified.
                    Urgent below marks the five items where the close date itself
                    fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards; it
                    is not the same as the top-three ranking.


                    *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
                    facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing
                    packet was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated
                    as fallible synthesis.*

                    '
                source_version: 8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73

            available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


              - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
              out).

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

              - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

              - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
              Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

              - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.

              - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay''s engine on day 1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

              - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor''s assets)

              - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
              institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

              - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
              Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for
              its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

              - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
              is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.

              - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


              ## Assumptions


              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
              and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
              acquisition without new state approval

              - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

              - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap

              - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to
              state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).

              - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).

              '

            available_excerpt: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter
              dossier)


              Matter MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated Sep
              9–10, 2026. Business question supplied by the matter record; direction
              unchanged.


              ## Current position


              Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review before
              the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before the deal terms
              are settled, not merely before launch. This is not "just a data migration":
              the day-1 plan depends on results the records show are unconfirmed —
              license coverage in the added markets, the ability to rely on Harbor''s
              KYC without the underlying records, and a monitoring cutover with no
              gap.


              Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


              - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day 1.**
              The plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established for an asset
              purchase. If approvals are missing, those markets are a post-close target,
              not day-1 access. (The number of added states is itself unresolved —
              see Record conflicts.)


              - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit reliance
              on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort with missing
              documents can keep full access without re-verification or limits.


              - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether
              monitoring transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the most
              decision-changing item because it can affect deal protections and how
              affected customers are handled at migration.


              The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms side
              of the data move do not block close on today''s record, but each must
              be reviewed before its own go-live point and each needs documents not
              in the readable record.


              What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance
              data pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review protocol
              for the alerts/SARs. What should wait or change: launching the added
              markets on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding of users whose
              verification cannot be evidenced; the monitoring cutover unless a tested
              no-gap design or a bridge exists; the bonus until its terms are reviewed.


              This draft recommends treating those items as pre-close gates and preparing
              a staged launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s recommendation,
              not a recorded decision. The recorded plan is unchanged: day-1 full
              migration, no re-verification, use/assume Harbor''s licenses, bonus
              at close+1. The only recorded lawyer decisions are the Sep 9 intake
              answers (asset purchase; compliance to confirm KYC reliance; alerts/SARs
              unreviewed; use/assume Harbor''s licenses). A complete dossier rewrite
              was submitted as a tracked revision on Sep 10 and, per the record, left
              the current dossier unchanged pending acceptance; generating this draft
              records no new decision.


              ## Decision question


              Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
              before the Nov 15 close?


              ## Issues


              The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the Sep 9
              initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s "four
              issues" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing, KYC/AML,
              alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list and its ISS
              identifiers were not inside this run''s readable material, so no issue
              IDs or markers are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly identified in
              this draft from the recorded migration plan, is included and labeled.


              Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable
              records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources
              ([source:MSG-20260909-660683], [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an initial
              "research is in progress" statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d]) later
              corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec], [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]),
              and a run described as "queued or running" with saved source choices
              ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output was readable here. Every
              legal proposition below is therefore a framework or lead, not verified
              support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**. Each issue gets
              an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers in the nine captured
              documents were not readable in this run and should be merged when available.


              ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


              **Current answer**


              Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically
              carry Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate
              legal entity cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses. Until
              a state-by-state path exists — new license, transfer or change-of-control
              approval in the transaction, or an arrangement where the licensed entity
              performs the transmission — the added markets should be treated as post-close,
              not part of day-1 full access. Even where Mosaic holds its own license,
              the account migration may trigger state notices or filings (unverified).


              **Rule and support**


              State money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or status
              as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money for others;
              licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state approval is commonly
              required for a change of control or transfer of a licensed business
              [**Needs checking** — the MTL statutes of the specific states; the CSBS
              Money Transmission Modernization Act where adopted]. Federal MSB registration
              (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380) is a separate requirement and does not substitute
              for state licensure [**Needs checking**]. The precise research question:
              for each state where Mosaic lacks a license and Harbor holds one, what
              route lets Mosaic lawfully serve migrated customers — new license, license
              transfer, change-of-control approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement
              — on what timeline, and what customer or regulator notices accompany
              the change?


              **Application**


              Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
              Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
              licenses"; full acce'
