            **Reported facts:** [facts.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md)\n-
            **Original request:** [request.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/request.md)\n-
            **Prior dossier revision:** [DOS-c993ab2326efd727cc3d.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier-revisions/DOS-c993ab2326efd727cc3d.md)\n\n<!--
            saved-issue-analysis:start -->\n## Saved issue answers\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
            -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
            under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive
            the acquisition\n\nDo not rely on transferability without an applicable
            state rule, approval, or written regulator position.\n\nThe answer must
            be determined state by state and must cover more than technical change-of-control
            rules.\n\nThis path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider
            and the relevant states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account
            design may conflict with that position.\n\nThe result depends on the contracts
            and actual funds flow. Custody alone should not be treated as a licensing
            exemption or transfer mechanism.\n\nResearch saved. 4 sources retrieved;
            0 with passages read.\n\nNext step: Identify the four Harbor-only states
            and complete one matrix covering license authority, transaction filings,
            interim operation, bank custody, outstanding obligations, and license
            surrender.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Detailed analysis</summary>\n\n**Practical
            answer**\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets
            that move to Mosaic in the asset purchase.** Use this closing rule:\n\n>
            **No confirmed authority means no regulated launch by Mosaic in that state.**\n\nThe
            asset purchase can still close. However, Mosaic should not activate regulated
            services in the four Harbor-only states unless one of these conditions
            is met:\n\n1. Mosaic obtains its own license.\n2. The state approves a
            transfer or other license change.\n3. The regulator confirms a lawful
            interim structure.\n4. Harbor remains the real licensed provider under
            a valid transition plan.\n5. Mosaic blocks regulated functions in that
            state.\n\nThe planned unified Mosaic account is important. It suggests
            that Mosaic, not Harbor, will become the service provider. If that is
            correct, keeping Harbor’s legal entity and licenses alive might not give
            Mosaic authority to operate.\n\n**No verified operative authority retrieved.**
            The collection found the CSBS Model Money Transmission Modernization Act
            and a New York regulator licensing page. However, no exact provision about
            an asset sale, license transfer, interim operation, or custody was available
            for review. Also, a model act is not proof of the law adopted in a specific
            state. The state-specific conclusions below remain conditional.\n\n**Work
            needed before launch**\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by |
            Evidence to proceed | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Identify
            the four Harbor-only states | These states have the clearest authority
            gap | Licensing team | Now | Confirmed license list and covered activities
            | Block regulated functions in those states |\n| Build a matrix for every
            affected state | Transfer, notice, approval, and surrender rules can differ
            | State regulatory counsel | Before the closing conditions are final |
            Applicable rule, filing deadline, regulator response, and license status
            | Delay migration in the affected state |\n| Confirm the post-close service
            provider | The licensed entity must match the actual operating model |
            Product and deal counsel | Before customer notices and account design
            are final | Contracts, user interface, funds-flow diagram, and operating
            roles | Keep Harbor as the actual provider where permitted |\n| Review
            notices and approvals | An asset sale can create separate seller and buyer
            requirements | Licensing team | Before each state deadline | Filing receipts
            and required approvals or non-objections | Make approval a state launch
            condition |\n| Confirm interim operating authority | A pending application
            should not be assumed to permit operation | State regulatory counsel |
            Before close | Applicable rule or written regulator confirmation | Keep
            Harbor customers segregated or restrict transactions |\n| Review partner-bank
            arrangements | Bank custody does not, by itself, establish Mosaic’s licensing
            position | Payments counsel and bank relationship owner | Before balances
            move | Bank agreements, account titles, control rights, reconciliation
            design, and bank consent | Keep funds and obligations in the existing
            structure |\n| Prepare license run-off and surrender plans | Harbor may
            retain duties for balances, claims, records, and reports | Harbor compliance
            and deal counsel | Before surrender or operational shutdown | Regulator-approved
            plan and continued bonds and financial coverage | Keep Harbor licensed
            and operational longer |\n\n**State notice and approval**\n\nDo not search
            only for a rule called “license transfer.” Review each state for:\n\n-
            sale of substantially all assets;\n- change of control;\n- change in business
            plan;\n- change in licensed activities;\n- assignment of outstanding payment
            obligations;\n- change in responsible persons, locations, or agents;\n-
            license surrender or termination;\n- customer agreement assignment; and\n-
            movement of stored balances or customer funds.\n\nAn asset purchase might
            fall outside a technical “change of control” rule because Harbor’s ownership
            does not change. That does not resolve the issue. Harbor might still need
            a notice or surrender approval. Mosaic might separately need authority
            before it starts the regulated activity.\n\nThe state matrix should distinguish:\n\n-
            notice only;\n- approval before closing;\n- approval before customer migration;\n-
            new license required;\n- operation permitted while an application is pending;\n-
            regulator-approved transition available; and\n- no supported interim path.\n\n**Interim
            operation**\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed provider for a transition
            period. However, the structure must be real, not only contractual language.\n\nA
            supportable structure would normally need to show that:\n\n- Harbor remains
            responsible to customers.\n- Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.\n-
            Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.\n- Harbor’s licenses,
            bonds, and financial coverage remain active.\n- Customer funds and outstanding
            obligations remain covered.\n- Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints,
            and examinations.\n- Required records remain available.\n- Mosaic’s operational
            role is permitted.\n- The partner bank accepts the structure.\n- Each
            relevant regulator permits or accepts the structure.\n\nThe present plan
            creates tension with this approach. A single Mosaic account, one combined
            balance, and full access to Mosaic products make it harder to show that
            Harbor remains the true provider.\n\n**Partner-bank custody**\n\nA partner
            bank account is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter
            license. The key questions concern the complete activity and obligation
            flow.\n\nFor each customer balance and transfer, document:\n\n1. Who receives
            the customer’s instruction?\n2. Who accepts the obligation to transmit
            or return the funds?\n3. In whose name is the bank account held?\n4. Is
            it a custodial or “for benefit of” account?\n5. Who can direct withdrawals?\n6.
            Who owns the ledger and resolves errors?\n7. Who bears loss if a transfer
            fails?\n8. Which entity owes the customer a refund?\n9. Which entity’s
            license, bond, and permissible investments cover the obligation?\n10.
            Does the bank agreement permit assignment, migration, or a change in the
            program manager?\n11. Is bank consent required before closing or migration?\n12.
            What happens to funds if Harbor, Mosaic, or the bank relationship ends?\n\nA
            bank-led model might provide a different licensing analysis if the bank
            is the actual provider and Mosaic performs only permitted services. A
            bank account that merely holds funds for Mosaic or Harbor is different.
            The legal documents, customer terms, control rights, and actual operations
            must all support the claimed model.\n\nAlso review:\n\n- account segregation;\n-
            daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve funding;\n- bank setoff
            rights;\n- liens and security interests;\n- continuity if the account
            is frozen;\n- treatment of pending transfers;\n- return and chargeback
            duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n- customer disclosures; and\n- whether
            any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account structure.\n\n**Recommended
            closing position**\n\nKeep the acquisition closing separate from the regulated-service
            launch.\n\nFor the four Harbor-only states, use a state launch hold unless
            Mosaic has documented authority. For overlapping states, confirm that
            Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the complete post-close product set and
            funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s licenses or release its bonds
            until the applicable regulators permit it and all outstanding obligations
            have been assigned, completed, or placed into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis
            investigation does not change the current recommendation. It adds one
            material point: **partner-bank custody is part of the licensing analysis,
            but custody alone does not cure an authority gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch
            history: [Saved research 1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n<!--
            issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045 -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether
            relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with missing underlying documents for pre-2023
            users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's independent CIP/AML obligations\n\nNo
            separate current answer is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial answer — research
            not complete.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38 -->\n### SAR
            and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor's ~40
            open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n\nNo separate current answer
            is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial answer — research not complete.\n\n<!--
            issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542 -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition:
            continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract terminates
            at close\n\nNo separate current answer is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial
            answer — research not complete.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
            -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
            money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\nNo separate
            current answer is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial answer — research not
            complete.\n<!-- saved-issue-analysis:end -->\n\nDossier preview generated;
            no matter records changed.\n\nIncluded full saved answers for 5 issue(s)."

        available_excerpt: "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe
          Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the targeted
          Nov 15 close. This is the accepted working view, not a recorded decision.\n\nMosaic
          plans to buy Harbor’s assets and move 240,000 consumer users and 12,000
          business accounts into one Mosaic account on day one. The main obstacles
          are:\n\n1. Mosaic has not shown that it can use Harbor’s licenses in the
          four Harbor-only states.\n2. Mosaic has not confirmed that Harbor’s prior
          know-your-customer (KYC) results satisfy Mosaic’s anti-money-laundering
          (AML) program.\n3. Harbor’s approximately 40 open alerts and recent suspicious
          activity report (SAR) history remain unread.\n4. The current monitoring
          service ends at close, and the replacement feed has not been shown to work.\n5.
          The terms of the $50 welcome bonus are not known.\n\nThe current direction
          remains unchanged. A full day-one migration is the planning baseline, but
          the saved working view supports launch restrictions where these conditions
          are not resolved. No decisions are recorded.\n\nThe analysis assumes that
          Harbor and Mosaic conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that
          Mosaic will become the operating provider immediately after close. It does
          not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that Harbor’s KYC records are
          sufficient, or that the monitoring change will work without a gap.\n\nA
          newer reported answer confirms that the deal is an asset purchase. It replaces
          the earlier assumption that the deal structure was unknown.\n\n## Decision
          question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
          review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n## Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
          under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nMosaic should not rely on Harbor’s
          money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically move to Mosaic.
          Before Mosaic starts regulated services in a state, it needs documented
          authority for the complete post-close activity in that state.\n\nThe asset
          purchase may close separately from the service launch. For the four Harbor-only
          states, the current working position is to hold regulated functions unless
          Mosaic has its own license, required state approval, a supported interim
          structure, or another documented basis to operate.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe
          saved research concludes that the answer must be determined state by state.
          The review must cover Mosaic’s authority, Harbor’s notices or approvals,
          outstanding obligations, interim operation, and license surrender.\n\nFour
          sources were retrieved, but no relevant passages were read or verified.
          The saved materials therefore do not establish an operative state rule:\n\n-
          [Research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
          [CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — retrieved, passage not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538-157583424427.md)\n-
          [New York Department of Financial Services licensing page — retrieved, passage
          not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fa80c95c5393.md)\n\nThe
          model act is not proof of the law in any specific state.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor
          reportedly holds licenses in 38 states. Mosaic reportedly holds licenses
          in 41 states. The proposed combined footprint has 44 states and would open
          four new markets. Mosaic currently plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses
          in those markets. The deal is an asset purchase.\n\nThe unified Mosaic account,
          combined balance, and access to Mosaic products suggest that Mosaic may
          become the actual provider. If so, keeping Harbor’s entity or licenses active
          might not give Mosaic authority. A transition in which Harbor remains the
          licensed provider could be possible only if the contracts, funds flow, customer
          terms, operating control, and applicable state requirements support that
          result.\n\nBank custody alone would not establish that Mosaic can perform
          the regulated activity. The full allocation of customer obligations and
          transfer control remains material.\n\n**Next step**\n\nIdentify the four
          Harbor-only states. Prepare one state matrix covering:\n\n- Mosaic’s authority
          for each post-close activity;\n- required transaction notices and approvals;\n-
          whether interim operation is permitted;\n- outstanding customer obligations;\n-
          bank custody and control;\n- Harbor’s run-off duties; and\n- license surrender
          requirements.\n\nDo not activate regulated functions in a state without
          documented authority.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start
          -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nDo

          In whose name is the bank account held?\n4. Is it a custodial or “for benefit

          resolves errors?\n7. Who bears loss if a transfer fails?\n8. Which entity

          account segregation;\n- daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve

          if the account is frozen;\n- treatment of pending transfers;\n- return and
          chargeback duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n- customer disclosures; and\n-
          whether any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account

          separate from the regulated-service launch.\n\nFor the four Harbor-only
          states, use a state launch hold unless Mosaic has documented authority.
          For overlapping states, confirm that Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the
          complete post-close product set and funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s
          licenses or release its bonds until the applicable regulators permit it
          and all outstanding obligations have been assigned, completed, or placed
          into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis investigation does not change
          the current recommendation. It adds one material point: **partner-bank custody
          is part of the licensing analysis, but custody alone does not cure an authority
          gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch history: [Saved research 1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n</details>\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
          -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with missing
          underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's independent
          CIP/AML obligations\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe current no-reverification
          plan is not yet supported. Mosaic’s compliance team has not confirmed that
          its AML and customer identification program permits reliance on Harbor’s
          prior KYC results.\n\nThe missing documents prove a record gap. They do
          not, by themselves, prove that identification was not completed or that
          a violation occurred.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe applicable rule depends
          on Mosaic’s legal status, its AML program, the permitted form of reliance,
          and the records that must remain available. This issue has not been researched.
          No saved authority establishes that Harbor’s pass/fail results are sufficient
          or insufficient.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s KYC vendor closed in 2024.
          Mosaic has pass/fail results for all users but lacks underlying documents
          for users onboarded before 2023. Mosaic plans to migrate the users without
          re-verification.\n\nWhether that is supportable depends on what Harbor collected,
          which records remain available, whether Mosaic can lawfully rely on Harbor’s
          process, and what Mosaic’s own program requires. The saved record does not
          answer these points.\n\n**Next step**\n\nCompliance should compare the available
          Harbor records with Mosaic’s program requirements. The evidence needed is:\n\n-
          Harbor’s KYC procedures and historical requirements;\n- available customer
          data and verification results;\n- the affected user count;\n- record-retention
          and access terms;\n- Mosaic’s reliance and remediation rules; and\n- a documented
          plan for users whose records are insufficient.\n\nUntil then, Mosaic should
          consider restrictions or staged access for affected users rather than assume
          that all prior KYC is sufficient.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:start
          -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38
          -->\n### SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
          Harbor's ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n\n**Current
          answer**\n\nThe alert and SAR review is a pre-close diligence priority.
          The saved record does not support a conclusion about filing duties, inherited
          liability, or whether any customer presents a material risk because nobody
          has reviewed the relevant history.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe responsible
          entity’s duties depend on the activity dates, transaction history, filing
          deadlines, deal terms, post-close operating roles, and applicable AML rules.
          This issue has not been researched.\n\nAccess to SAR information can be
          legally restricted. Diligence must distinguish permitted review from disclosure
          or transfer of protected material.\n\n**Application**\n\nDiligence found
          approximately 40 open alerts and a handful of SARs from the prior year.
          They remain unread. This creates an information gap about unresolved suspicious
          activity, overdue review, affected accounts, and any needed post-close controls.\n\nThe
          asset purchase does not, on the saved material, answer which entity must
          finish each alert or make any required filing.\n\n**Next step**\n\nArrange
          a legally permitted review before migration. Create a case list showing:\n\n-
          alert age and status;\n- affected account;\n- transactions involved;\n-
          required decision or escalation;\n- filing status and deadline, if any;\n-
          responsible pre-close and post-close entity; and\n- any required account
          restriction.\n\nEscalate material findings into the closing and migration
          conditions.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:start

          -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
          when the SaaS contract terminates at close\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
          monitoring transition should be tested and accepted before migrated users
          receive full product access. The saved assumption that repointing will work
          without a monitoring gap remains open.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nIf Mosaic’s
          applicable AML program requires transaction monitoring, its implemented
          controls must cover the activities and users that move to Mosaic. The exact
          requirements and any permitted transition measures have not been researched.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s
          monitoring software contract ends at close. Mosaic plans to repoint Harbor’s
          transaction feed to Mosaic’s engine on day one. The current record contains
          no test results, data mapping, alert validation, capacity review, or fallback
          plan.\n\nA technical connection alone would not show that Mosaic’s rules
          detect the relevant Harbor activity or that no transactions are lost during
          the change.\n\n**Next step**\n\nComplete an end-to-end test before migration.
          Evidence should include:\n\n- all expected transaction types and fields;\n-
          successful data reconciliation;\n- rule coverage for Harbor products;\n-
          test alerts and case creation;\n- operating ownership;\n- cutover and rollback
          procedures; and\n- monitoring coverage during any outage.\n\nIf the test
          does not pass, continue the existing service if possible or limit the affected
          transactions until monitoring is effective.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:start

          -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
          money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
          welcome bonus needs review before release, but it is lower priority than
          licensing and AML readiness. The saved record does not contain enough information

          limits, and the accuracy of the advertising. This issue has not been researched.\n\n**Application**\n\nMarketing

          -->\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n<!-- alternative:SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4
          -->\n### Bank-held funds timing test — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved
          alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
          this test only:\n\n- A bank would hold the relevant funds.\n- Mosaic would
          control transfer instructions.\n- The structure depends on completing the
          bank contract and operating setup.\n- Migration would occur on November
          15, 2026.\n- Bank integration would be ready on December 3, 2026.\n- Pre-2023
          identity documents would remain missing.\n- Forty alert cases would remain
          pending.\n- The monitoring service would end at close.\n\nThese dates and
          conditions are test facts only. They do not change the actual close record
          or current direction.\n\n**Benefits**\n\nBank custody could support a different
          operating structure if the bank is the actual provider and the contracts,
          customer terms, control rights, and operations support that position. The
          saved test does not establish that result.\n\n**Trade-offs and added risks**\n\nOn
          the test dates, bank integration would not be ready until 18 days after
          the planned November 15 migration. This makes the alternative harder to
          use for that migration.\n\nMosaic would still control transfer instructions.
          The saved material does not show that bank custody alone changes Mosaic’s
          licensing position. Failure to complete the bank contract or operating setup
          in time would prevent use of this option on the test date.\n\n**Issues that
          remain**\n\nThe alternative does not resolve:\n\n- missing pre-2023 identity
          documents;\n- 40 pending alert cases;\n- monitoring ending at close;\n-
          Mosaic’s authority for its actual role;\n- customer contract terms; or\n-
          allocation of AML and reporting duties.\n\n**Next action**\n\nProposed,
          not assigned: Mara Chen should obtain a dated bank-readiness plan and confirm
          whether the bank can support November 15, 2026. The plan should also assign
          work for the identity records, pending alerts, and replacement monitoring.\n\n<!--
          alternative:SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6 -->\n### Bank-held funds structure
          — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
          this test only, a partner bank would hold customer funds. The recorded acquisition
          remains an asset purchase.\n\n**Benefits**\n\nA bank-led model could produce
          a different money-transmission analysis if the bank were the actual provider
          and Mosaic performed only permitted services. The saved alternative does
          not establish these facts.\n\n**Trade-offs and added risks**\n\nThe structure
          would require contracts and operations that match the claimed bank role.
          It could add dependencies for bank consent, account setup, operating control,
          reconciliation, customer terms, and service continuity.\n\nNo saved working
          note or test evidence establishes readiness or a timing benefit.\n\n**Issues
          that remain**\n\nThe following points are unresolved:\n\n- who contracts
          directly with users;\n- who controls transfer instructions and settlement;\n-
          who records balances and owes repayment;\n- how KYC and monitoring duties
          are allocated;\n- who handles alerts and SARs;\n- how privacy duties are
          allocated; and\n- who is responsible for the welcome bonus.\n\nHolding funds
          at a bank does not, on the saved material, resolve these issues.\n\n**Next
          action**\n\nProposed, not assigned: prepare a funds-flow and responsibility
          map. Obtain the bank agreements, customer terms, account titles, control
          rights, settlement process, loss allocation, and bank consent requirements
          before comparing this structure with the current plan.\n\n## Next actions\n\n1.
          **Complete the four-state licensing matrix.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed;
          no assignment recorded.  \n   **Proposed owners:** Licensing team and state
          regulatory counsel.  \n   **Date:** Before the targeted Nov 15 close; no
          separate due date or year is recorded for this action.  \n   **Evidence
          needed:** Applicable state rules, filing deadlines, regulator responses,
          Mosaic and Harbor license status, post-close funds flow, and any interim
          authority.\n\n2. **Review Harbor’s open alerts and SAR history through a
          permitted diligence process.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment
          recorded.  \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded.  \n   **Date:** Before migration;
          no due date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Case inventory, age, status,
          filing history, responsible entity, deadlines, and account-control decisions.\n\n3.
          **Decide whether Mosaic’s AML and customer identification program permits
          reliance on Harbor’s KYC.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment recorded.
          \ \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded; compliance confirmation is required
          by the saved facts.  \n   **Date:** Before migration; no due date recorded.
          \ \n   **Evidence needed:** Mosaic’s program requirements, Harbor’s procedures,
          available customer records, affected user count, and remediation criteria.\n\n4.
          **Test the monitoring cutover.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment
          recorded.  \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded.  \n   **Date:** Before migration;
          no due date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Reconciliation results,
          rule coverage, test alerts, ownership, outage coverage, and rollback plan.\n\n5.
          **Review the welcome-bonus structure and advertising.**  \n   **Status:**
          Proposed; no assignment recorded.  \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded.  \n
          \  **Date:** Before the planned close+1 launch; no due date recorded.  \n
          \  **Evidence needed:** Final terms, funding flow, eligibility, restrictions,

          content: "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe Harbor
            Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the targeted Nov
            15 close. This is the accepted working view, not a recorded decision.\n\nMosaic
            plans to buy Harbor’s assets and move 240,000 consumer users and 12,000
            business accounts into one Mosaic account on day one. The main obstacles
            are:\n\n1. Mosaic has not shown that it can use Harbor’s licenses in the
            four Harbor-only states.\n2. Mosaic has not confirmed that Harbor’s prior
            know-your-customer (KYC) results satisfy Mosaic’s anti-money-laundering
            (AML) program.\n3. Harbor’s approximately 40 open alerts and recent suspicious
            activity report (SAR) history remain unread.\n4. The current monitoring
            service ends at close, and the replacement feed has not been shown to
            work.\n5. The terms of the $50 welcome bonus are not known.\n\nThe current
            direction remains unchanged. A full day-one migration is the planning
            baseline, but the saved working view supports launch restrictions where
            these conditions are not resolved. No decisions are recorded.\n\nThe analysis
            assumes that Harbor and Mosaic conduct regulated money-transmission activity
            and that Mosaic will become the operating provider immediately after close.
            It does not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that Harbor’s KYC
            records are sufficient, or that the monitoring change will work without
            a gap.\n\nA newer reported answer confirms that the deal is an asset purchase.
            It replaces the earlier assumption that the deal structure was unknown.\n\n##
            Decision question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration
            need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n## Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
            -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
            under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive
            the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nMosaic should not rely on Harbor’s
            money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically move to Mosaic.
            Before Mosaic starts regulated services in a state, it needs documented
            authority for the complete post-close activity in that state.\n\nThe asset
            purchase may close separately from the service launch. For the four Harbor-only
            states, the current working position is to hold regulated functions unless
            Mosaic has its own license, required state approval, a supported interim
            structure, or another documented basis to operate.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe
            saved research concludes that the answer must be determined state by state.
            The review must cover Mosaic’s authority, Harbor’s notices or approvals,
            outstanding obligations, interim operation, and license surrender.\n\nFour
            sources were retrieved, but no relevant passages were read or verified.
            The saved materials therefore do not establish an operative state rule:\n\n-
            [Research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
            [CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — retrieved, passage not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538-157583424427.md)\n-
            [New York Department of Financial Services licensing page — retrieved,
            passage not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fa80c95c5393.md)\n\nThe
            model act is not proof of the law in any specific state.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor
            reportedly holds licenses in 38 states. Mosaic reportedly holds licenses
            in 41 states. The proposed combined footprint has 44 states and would
            open four new markets. Mosaic currently plans to use or assume Harbor’s
            licenses in those markets. The deal is an asset purchase.\n\nThe unified
            Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products suggest
            that Mosaic may become the actual provider. If so, keeping Harbor’s entity
            or licenses active might not give Mosaic authority. A transition in which
            Harbor remains the licensed provider could be possible only if the contracts,
            funds flow, customer terms, operating control, and applicable state requirements
            support that result.\n\nBank custody alone would not establish that Mosaic
            can perform the regulated activity. The full allocation of customer obligations
            and transfer control remains material.\n\n**Next step**\n\nIdentify the
            four Harbor-only states. Prepare one state matrix covering:\n\n- Mosaic’s
            authority for each post-close activity;\n- required transaction notices
            and approvals;\n- whether interim operation is permitted;\n- outstanding
            customer obligations;\n- bank custody and control;\n- Harbor’s run-off
            duties; and\n- license surrender requirements.\n\nDo not activate regulated
            functions in a state without documented authority.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start
            -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nDo
            not rely on transferability without an applicable state rule, approval,
            or written regulator position.\n\nThe answer must be determined state
            by state and must cover more than technical change-of-control rules.\n\nThis
            path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider and the relevant
            states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account design may conflict
            with that position.\n\nThe result depends on the contracts and actual
            funds flow. Custody alone should not be treated as a licensing exemption
            or transfer mechanism.\n\nResearch saved. 4 sources retrieved; 0 with
            passages read.\n\nNext step: Identify the four Harbor-only states and
            complete one matrix covering license authority, transaction filings, interim
            operation, bank custody, outstanding obligations, and license surrender.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Detailed
            analysis</summary>\n\n**Practical answer**\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s
            money transmitter licenses as assets that move to Mosaic in the asset
            purchase.** Use this closing rule:\n\n> **No confirmed authority means
            no regulated launch by Mosaic in that state.**\n\nThe asset purchase can
            still close. However, Mosaic should not activate regulated services in
            the four Harbor-only states unless one of these conditions is met:\n\n1.
            Mosaic obtains its own license.\n2. The state approves a transfer or other
            license change.\n3. The regulator confirms a lawful interim structure.\n4.
            Harbor remains the real licensed provider under a valid transition plan.\n5.
            Mosaic blocks regulated functions in that state.\n\nThe planned unified
            Mosaic account is important. It suggests that Mosaic, not Harbor, will
            become the service provider. If that is correct, keeping Harbor’s legal
            entity and licenses alive might not give Mosaic authority to operate.\n\n**No
            verified operative authority retrieved.** The collection found the CSBS
            Model Money Transmission Modernization Act and a New York regulator licensing
            page. However, no exact provision about an asset sale, license transfer,
            interim operation, or custody was available for review. Also, a model
            act is not proof of the law adopted in a specific state. The state-specific
            conclusions below remain conditional.\n\n**Work needed before launch**\n\n|
            Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence to proceed | Fallback
            |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Identify the four Harbor-only states |
            These states have the clearest authority gap | Licensing team | Now |
            Confirmed license list and covered activities | Block regulated functions
            in those states |\n| Build a matrix for every affected state | Transfer,
            notice, approval, and surrender rules can differ | State regulatory counsel
            | Before the closing conditions are final | Applicable rule, filing deadline,
            regulator response, and license status | Delay migration in the affected
            state |\n| Confirm the post-close service provider | The licensed entity
            must match the actual operating model | Product and deal counsel | Before
            customer notices and account design are final | Contracts, user interface,
            funds-flow diagram, and operating roles | Keep Harbor as the actual provider
            where permitted |\n| Review notices and approvals | An asset sale can
            create separate seller and buyer requirements | Licensing team | Before
            each state deadline | Filing receipts and required approvals or non-objections
            | Make approval a state launch condition |\n| Confirm interim operating
            authority | A pending application should not be assumed to permit operation
            | State regulatory counsel | Before close | Applicable rule or written
            regulator confirmation | Keep Harbor customers segregated or restrict
            transactions |\n| Review partner-bank arrangements | Bank custody does
            not, by itself, establish Mosaic’s licensing position | Payments counsel
            and bank relationship owner | Before balances move | Bank agreements,
            account titles, control rights, reconciliation design, and bank consent
            | Keep funds and obligations in the existing structure |\n| Prepare license
            run-off and surrender plans | Harbor may retain duties for balances, claims,
            records, and reports | Harbor compliance and deal counsel | Before surrender
            or operational shutdown | Regulator-approved plan and continued bonds
            and financial coverage | Keep Harbor licensed and operational longer |\n\n**State
            notice and approval**\n\nDo not search only for a rule called “license
            transfer.” Review each state for:\n\n- sale of substantially all assets;\n-
            change of control;\n- change in business plan;\n- change in licensed activities;\n-
            assignment of outstanding payment obligations;\n- change in responsible
            persons, locations, or agents;\n- license surrender or termination;\n-
            customer agreement assignment; and\n- movement of stored balances or customer
            funds.\n\nAn asset purchase might fall outside a technical “change of
            control” rule because Harbor’s ownership does not change. That does not
            resolve the issue. Harbor might still need a notice or surrender approval.
            Mosaic might separately need authority before it starts the regulated
            activity.\n\nThe state matrix should distinguish:\n\n- notice only;\n-
            approval before closing;\n- approval before customer migration;\n- new
            license required;\n- operation permitted while an application is pending;\n-
            regulator-approved transition available; and\n- no supported interim path.\n\n**Interim
            operation**\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed provider for a transition
            period. However, the structure must be real, not only contractual language.\n\nA
            supportable structure would normally need to show that:\n\n- Harbor remains
            responsible to customers.\n- Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.\n-
            Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.\n- Harbor’s licenses,
            bonds, and financial coverage remain active.\n- Customer funds and outstanding
            obligations remain covered.\n- Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints,
            and examinations.\n- Required records remain available.\n- Mosaic’s operational
            role is permitted.\n- The partner bank accepts the structure.\n- Each
            relevant regulator permits or accepts the structure.\n\nThe present plan
            creates tension with this approach. A single Mosaic account, one combined
            balance, and full access to Mosaic products make it harder to show that
            Harbor remains the true provider.\n\n**Partner-bank custody**\n\nA partner
            bank account is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter
            license. The key questions concern the complete activity and obligation
            flow.\n\nFor each customer balance and transfer, document:\n\n1. Who receives
            the customer’s instruction?\n2. Who accepts the obligation to transmit
            or return the funds?\n3. In whose name is the bank account held?\n4. Is
            it a custodial or “for benefit of” account?\n5. Who can direct withdrawals?\n6.
            Who owns the ledger and resolves errors?\n7. Who bears loss if a transfer
            fails?\n8. Which entity owes the customer a refund?\n9. Which entity’s
            license, bond, and permissible investments cover the obligation?\n10.
            Does the bank agreement permit assignment, migration, or a change in the
            program manager?\n11. Is bank consent required before closing or migration?\n12.
            What happens to funds if Harbor, Mosaic, or the bank relationship ends?\n\nA
            bank-led model might provide a different licensing analysis if the bank
            is the actual provider and Mosaic performs only permitted services. A
            bank account that merely holds funds for Mosaic or Harbor is different.
            The legal documents, customer terms, control rights, and actual operations
            must all support the claimed model.\n\nAlso review:\n\n- account segregation;\n-
            daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve funding;\n- bank setoff
            rights;\n- liens and security interests;\n- continuity if the account
            is frozen;\n- treatment of pending transfers;\n- return and chargeback
            duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n- customer disclosures; and\n- whether
            any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account structure.\n\n**Recommended
            closing position**\n\nKeep the acquisition closing separate from the regulated-service
            launch.\n\nFor the four Harbor-only states, use a state launch hold unless
            Mosaic has documented authority. For overlapping states, confirm that
            Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the complete post-close product set and
            funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s licenses or release its bonds
            until the applicable regulators permit it and all outstanding obligations
            have been assigned, completed, or placed into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis
            investigation does not change the current recommendation. It adds one
            material point: **partner-bank custody is part of the licensing analysis,
            but custody alone does not cure an authority gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch
            history: [Saved research 1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n</details>\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
            -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with
            missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's
            independent CIP/AML obligations\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe current no-reverification
            plan is not yet supported. Mosaic’s compliance team has not confirmed
            that its AML and customer identification program permits reliance on Harbor’s
            prior KYC results.\n\nThe missing documents prove a record gap. They do
            not, by themselves, prove that identification was not completed or that
            a violation occurred.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe applicable rule depends
            on Mosaic’s legal status, its AML program, the permitted form of reliance,
            and the records that must remain available. This issue has not been researched.
            No saved authority establishes that Harbor’s pass/fail results are sufficient
            or insufficient.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s KYC vendor closed in 2024.
            Mosaic has pass/fail results for all users but lacks underlying documents
            for users onboarded before 2023. Mosaic plans to migrate the users without
            re-verification.\n\nWhether that is supportable depends on what Harbor
            collected, which records remain available, whether Mosaic can lawfully
            rely on Harbor’s process, and what Mosaic’s own program requires. The
            saved record does not answer these points.\n\n**Next step**\n\nCompliance
            should compare the available Harbor records with Mosaic’s program requirements.
            The evidence needed is:\n\n- Harbor’s KYC procedures and historical requirements;\n-
            available customer data and verification results;\n- the affected user
            count;\n- record-retention and access terms;\n- Mosaic’s reliance and
            remediation rules; and\n- a documented plan for users whose records are
            insufficient.\n\nUntil then, Mosaic should consider restrictions or staged
            access for affected users rather than assume that all prior KYC is sufficient.\n\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:start -->\nInitial analysis
            — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:end
            -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38 -->\n### SAR and alert
            handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor's ~40 open alerts
            and SARs, and successor liability\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe alert and
            SAR review is a pre-close diligence priority. The saved record does not
            support a conclusion about filing duties, inherited liability, or whether
            any customer presents a material risk because nobody has reviewed the
            relevant history.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe responsible entity’s
            duties depend on the activity dates, transaction history, filing deadlines,
            deal terms, post-close operating roles, and applicable AML rules. This
            issue has not been researched.\n\nAccess to SAR information can be legally
            restricted. Diligence must distinguish permitted review from disclosure
            or transfer of protected material.\n\n**Application**\n\nDiligence found
            approximately 40 open alerts and a handful of SARs from the prior year.
            They remain unread. This creates an information gap about unresolved suspicious
            activity, overdue review, affected accounts, and any needed post-close
            controls.\n\nThe asset purchase does not, on the saved material, answer
            which entity must finish each alert or make any required filing.\n\n**Next
            step**\n\nArrange a legally permitted review before migration. Create
            a case list showing:\n\n- alert age and status;\n- affected account;\n-
            transactions involved;\n- required decision or escalation;\n- filing status
            and deadline, if any;\n- responsible pre-close and post-close entity;
            and\n- any required account restriction.\n\nEscalate material findings
            into the closing and migration conditions.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:start
            -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542
            -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
            when the SaaS contract terminates at close\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
            monitoring transition should be tested and accepted before migrated users
            receive full product access. The saved assumption that repointing will
            work without a monitoring gap remains open.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nIf
            Mosaic’s applicable AML program requires transaction monitoring, its implemented
            controls must cover the activities and users that move to Mosaic. The
            exact requirements and any permitted transition measures have not been
            researched.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s monitoring software contract
            ends at close. Mosaic plans to repoint Harbor’s transaction feed to Mosaic’s
            engine on day one. The current record contains no test results, data mapping,
            alert validation, capacity review, or fallback plan.\n\nA technical connection
            alone would not show that Mosaic’s rules detect the relevant Harbor activity
            or that no transactions are lost during the change.\n\n**Next step**\n\nComplete
            an end-to-end test before migration. Evidence should include:\n\n- all
            expected transaction types and fields;\n- successful data reconciliation;\n-
            rule coverage for Harbor products;\n- test alerts and case creation;\n-
            operating ownership;\n- cutover and rollback procedures; and\n- monitoring
            coverage during any outage.\n\nIf the test does not pass, continue the
            existing service if possible or limit the affected transactions until
            monitoring is effective.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:start
            -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
            -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
            money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
            welcome bonus needs review before release, but it is lower priority than
            licensing and AML readiness. The saved record does not contain enough
            information to determine the required terms or disclosures.\n\n**Rule
            and support**\n\nThe applicable requirements depend on how customers earn
            the bonus, who funds and pays it, any transfer or holding conditions,
            expiration terms, geographic limits, and the accuracy of the advertising.
            This issue has not been researched.\n\n**Application**\n\nMarketing wants
            to launch a $50 bonus on the first transfer at close+1. The structure
            remains unknown. It is not established whether the bonus is deposited
            into the account, applied as a credit, subject to repayment or forfeiture,
            or limited to particular customers or states.\n\nThe campaign also depends
            on Mosaic having authority to offer the underlying service in each market.\n\n**Next
            step**\n\nObtain the final offer terms, customer journey, funding flow,
            advertising copy, eligibility rules, exclusions, expiration terms, and
            state coverage. Review those materials before publication. Do not advertise
            service in a state where Mosaic’s operating authority remains unresolved.\n\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66:start -->\nInitial analysis
            — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66:end
            -->\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n<!-- alternative:SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4
            -->\n### Bank-held funds timing test — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved
            alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
            this test only:\n\n- A bank would hold the relevant funds.\n- Mosaic would
            control transfer instructions.\n- The structure depends on completing
            the bank contract and operating setup.\n- Migration would occur on November
            15, 2026.\n- Bank integration would be ready on December 3, 2026.\n- Pre-2023
            identity documents would remain missing.\n- Forty alert cases would remain
            pending.\n- The monitoring service would end at close.\n\nThese dates
            and conditions are test facts only. They do not change the actual close
            record or current direction.\n\n**Benefits**\n\nBank custody could support
            a different operating structure if the bank is the actual provider and
            the contracts, customer terms, control rights, and operations support
            that position. The saved test does not establish that result.\n\n**Trade-offs
            and added risks**\n\nOn the test dates, bank integration would not be
            ready until 18 days after the planned November 15 migration. This makes
            the alternative harder to use for that migration.\n\nMosaic would still
            control transfer instructions. The saved material does not show that bank
            custody alone changes Mosaic’s licensing position. Failure to complete
            the bank contract or operating setup in time would prevent use of this
            option on the test date.\n\n**Issues that remain**\n\nThe alternative
            does not resolve:\n\n- missing pre-2023 identity documents;\n- 40 pending
            alert cases;\n- monitoring ending at close;\n- Mosaic’s authority for
            its actual role;\n- customer contract terms; or\n- allocation of AML and
            reporting duties.\n\n**Next action**\n\nProposed, not assigned: Mara Chen
            should obtain a dated bank-readiness plan and confirm whether the bank
            can support November 15, 2026. The plan should also assign work for the
            identity records, pending alerts, and replacement monitoring.\n\n<!--
            alternative:SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6 -->\n### Bank-held funds structure
            — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
            this test only, a partner bank would hold customer funds. The recorded
            acquisition remains an asset purchase.\n\n**Benefits**\n\nA bank-led model
            could produce a different money-transmission analysis if the bank were
            the actual provider and Mosaic performed only permitted services. The
            saved alternative does not establish these facts.\n\n**Trade-offs and
            added risks**\n\nThe structure would require contracts and operations
            that match the claimed bank role. It could add dependencies for bank consent,
            account setup, operating control, reconciliation, customer terms, and
            service continuity.\n\nNo saved working note or test evidence establishes
            readiness or a timing benefit.\n\n**Issues that remain**\n\nThe following
            points are unresolved:\n\n- who contracts directly with users;\n- who
            controls transfer instructions and settlement;\n- who records balances
            and owes repayment;\n- how KYC and monitoring duties are allocated;\n-
            who handles alerts and SARs;\n- how privacy duties are allocated; and\n-
            who is responsible for the welcome bonus.\n\nHolding funds at a bank does
            not, on the saved material, resolve these issues.\n\n**Next action**\n\nProposed,
            not assigned: prepare a funds-flow and responsibility map. Obtain the
            bank agreements, customer terms, account titles, control rights, settlement
            process, loss allocation, and bank consent requirements before comparing
            this structure with the current plan.\n\n## Next actions\n\n1. **Complete
            the four-state licensing matrix.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment
            recorded.  \n   **Proposed owners:** Licensing team and state regulatory
            counsel.  \n   **Date:** Before the targeted Nov 15 close; no separate
            due date or year is recorded for this action.  \n   **Evidence needed:**
            Applicable state rules, filing deadlines, regulator responses, Mosaic
            and Harbor license status, post-close funds flow, and any interim authority.\n\n2.
            **Review Harbor’s open alerts and SAR history through a permitted diligence
            process.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment recorded.  \n   **Owner:**
            No owner recorded.  \n   **Date:** Before migration; no due date recorded.
            \ \n   **Evidence needed:** Case inventory, age, status, filing history,
            responsible entity, deadlines, and account-control decisions.\n\n3. **Decide
            whether Mosaic’s AML and customer identification program permits reliance
            on Harbor’s KYC.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment recorded.
            \ \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded; compliance confirmation is required
            by the saved facts.  \n   **Date:** Before migration; no due date recorded.
            \ \n   **Evidence needed:** Mosaic’s program requirements, Harbor’s procedures,
            available customer records, affected user count, and remediation criteria.\n\n4.
            **Test the monitoring cutover.**  \n   **Status:** Proposed; no assignment
            recorded.  \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded.  \n   **Date:** Before migration;
            no due date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Reconciliation results,
            rule coverage, test alerts, ownership, outage coverage, and rollback plan.\n\n5.
            **Review the welcome-bonus structure and advertising.**  \n   **Status:**
            Proposed; no assignment recorded.  \n   **Owner:** No owner recorded.
            \ \n   **Date:** Before the planned close+1 launch; no due date recorded.
            \ \n   **Evidence needed:** Final terms, funding flow, eligibility, restrictions,
            customer disclosures, advertising copy, and state coverage.\n\n## Current
            work product and supporting records\n\n- Current work product: No current
            draft or final path is saved.\n- [Latest licensing research](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
            [Known facts](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md)\n- [Original request](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/request.md)\n-

            [Bank-held funds structure](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6.md)\n\n[Open

            generated and saved."
