          The Harbor Pay migration needs l…'
        source_class: saved_artifact
        path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/conversations/CONV-20260909-5299cf.md
        available_excerpt: "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe
          Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
          Nov 15 close. This is the accepted working view. It is not a recorded decision.\n\nMosaic
          Relay plans an asset purchase. It then plans to move 240,000 consumer users
          and 12,000 business accounts into a unified Mosaic account on day one after
          close. Users would receive full access to Mosaic products.\n\nThe main obstacle
          is whether Mosaic has authority to provide each post-close service in every
          affected state. Mosaic should not assume that Harbor’s money transmitter
          licenses transfer with the purchased assets.\n\nThe other material obstacles
          are:\n\n- Mosaic has not confirmed whether its anti-money-laundering and
          customer identification program permits reliance on Harbor’s prior know-your-customer
          results.\n- Underlying identity documents are missing for users onboarded
          before 2023.\n- Harbor’s approximately 40 open alerts and recent suspicious
          activity report history have not been reviewed.\n- Harbor’s monitoring service
          ends at close. The replacement feed has not been validated.\n- The terms
          and operating structure of the planned $50 welcome bonus are unknown.\n\nThe
          full day-one migration remains the planning baseline. State launch holds,
          account restrictions, or delayed product access remain possible safeguards
          if the open conditions are not resolved. No decisions are recorded.\n\n###
          Assumptions used\n\n- Harbor is a licensed money transmitter subject to
          applicable state and federal anti-money-laundering requirements. This assumption
          affects the licensing, customer identification, alert, and monitoring analysis.\n-
          Mosaic will become the operating provider immediately after close. This
          affects whether Harbor can remain the licensed provider during a transition.\n-
          The analysis does not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that its prior
          identity checks satisfy Mosaic’s requirements, or that monitoring can continue
          without a gap.\n- Mosaic’s reported 41-state license footprint is treated
          as a reported fact.\n- The acquisition structure is no longer assumed to
          be unknown. The reported structure is an asset purchase.\n\n### Record conflicts\n\n-
          Mosaic reportedly has licenses in 41 states, and the combined footprint
          is 44 states. `44 − 41 = 3`, but the record says the acquisition opens four
          new markets. This affects which jurisdictions require new authority or launch
          restrictions. The license lists and the intended meaning of “market” are
          needed.\n- Matter metadata gives a target date of `2026-09-11`. The reported
          close is “Nov 15,” approximately ten weeks after the Sept. 9 intake. A saved
          hypothetical uses November 15, 2026, but that does not establish the actual
          closing year. The operative close date and year remain unresolved.\n\n##
          Decision question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration
          need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n## Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
          under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nMosaic should not treat Harbor’s
          money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically move to Mosaic in
          the asset purchase.\n\nThe acquisition may close separately from the service
          launch. Mosaic should not start regulated services in a state unless it
          has documented authority for the complete post-close activity.\n\n**Rule
          and support**\n\nThe saved research concludes that the answer must be determined
          state by state. Review must cover Mosaic’s operating authority, transaction
          notices and approvals, interim operation, outstanding obligations, and Harbor’s
          license surrender.\n\nFour sources were retrieved, but no relevant passages
          were read or verified. They do not establish an operative state rule:\n\n-
          [Research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
          [CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — retrieved, but relevant passage
          not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538-157583424427.md)\n-
          [New York Department of Financial Services licensing page — retrieved, but
          relevant passage not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fa80c95c5393.md)\n\nThe
          model act is not proof of the law in any specific state.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor
          reportedly has licenses in 38 states. Mosaic reportedly has licenses in
          41 states. Their combined footprint is reported as 44 states. Mosaic currently
          plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in the new markets.\n\nThe unified
          Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products suggest
          that Mosaic may become the actual service provider. If so, keeping Harbor’s
          entity or licenses active might not give Mosaic authority.\n\nA transition
          in which Harbor remains the licensed provider is possible only if the customer
          contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses, bonds, records, and
          applicable state rules support that result.\n\nA partner bank holding funds
          would not, by itself, establish Mosaic’s authority. The answer depends on
          who contracts with users, controls transfers, owes repayment, maintains
          balances, resolves errors, and carries the regulated duties.\n\n**Next step**\n\nIdentify
          the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare one state matrix covering:\n\n-
          Mosaic’s authority for each post-close activity;\n- notices, filings, approvals,
          and deadlines;\n- operation while an application is pending;\n- transfer
          of customer agreements and outstanding obligations;\n- bank custody and
          control;\n- Harbor’s run-off duties, bonds, and license surrender; and\n-
          the launch restriction needed if authority is not established.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start
          -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nDo
          not rely on transferability without an applicable state rule, approval,
          or written regulator position.\n\nThe answer must be determined state by
          state and must cover more than technical change-of-control rules.\n\nThis
          path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider and the relevant
          states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account design may conflict
          with that position.\n\nThe result depends on the contracts and actual funds
          flow. Custody alone should not be treated as a licensing exemption or transfer
          mechanism.\n\nResearch saved. 4 sources retrieved; 0 with passages read.\n\nNext
          step: Identify the four Harbor-only states and complete one matrix covering
          license authority, transaction filings, interim operation, bank custody,
          outstanding obligations, and license surrender.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Detailed
          analysis</summary>\n\n**Practical answer**\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s money
          transmitter licenses as assets that move to Mosaic in the asset purchase.**
          Use this closing rule:\n\n> **No confirmed authority means no regulated
          launch by Mosaic in that state.**\n\nThe asset purchase can still close.
          However, Mosaic should not activate regulated services in the four Harbor-only
          states unless one of these conditions is met:\n\n1. Mosaic obtains its own
          license.\n2. The state approves a transfer or other license change.\n3.
          The regulator confirms a lawful interim structure.\n4. Harbor remains the
          real licensed provider under a valid transition plan.\n5. Mosaic blocks
          regulated functions in that state.\n\nThe planned unified Mosaic account
          is important. It suggests that Mosaic, not Harbor, will become the service
          provider. If that is correct, keeping Harbor’s legal entity and licenses
          alive might not give Mosaic authority to operate.\n\n**No verified operative
          authority retrieved.** The collection found the CSBS Model Money Transmission
          Modernization Act and a New York regulator licensing page. However, no exact
          provision about an asset sale, license transfer, interim operation, or custody
          was available for review. Also, a model act is not proof of the law adopted
          in a specific state. The state-specific conclusions below remain conditional.\n\n**Work
          needed before launch**\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence
          to proceed | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Identify the four
          Harbor-only states | These states have the clearest authority gap | Licensing
          team | Now | Confirmed license list and covered activities | Block regulated
          functions in those states |\n| Build a matrix for every affected state |
          Transfer, notice, approval, and surrender rules can differ | State regulatory
          counsel | Before the closing conditions are final | Applicable rule, filing
          deadline, regulator response, and license status | Delay migration in the
          affected state |\n| Confirm the post-close service provider | The licensed
          entity must match the actual operating model | Product and deal counsel
          | Before customer notices and account design are final | Contracts, user
          interface, funds-flow diagram, and operating roles | Keep Harbor as the
          actual provider where permitted |\n| Review notices and approvals | An asset
          sale can create separate seller and buyer requirements | Licensing team
          | Before each state deadline | Filing receipts and required approvals or
          non-objections | Make approval a state launch condition |\n| Confirm interim
          operating authority | A pending application should not be assumed to permit
          operation | State regulatory counsel | Before close | Applicable rule or
          written regulator confirmation | Keep Harbor customers segregated or restrict
          transactions |\n| Review partner-bank arrangements | Bank custody does not,
          by itself, establish Mosaic’s licensing position | Payments counsel and
          bank relationship owner | Before balances move | Bank agreements, account
          titles, control rights, reconciliation design, and bank consent | Keep funds
          and obligations in the existing structure |\n| Prepare license run-off and
          surrender plans | Harbor may retain duties for balances, claims, records,
          and reports | Harbor compliance and deal counsel | Before surrender or operational
          shutdown | Regulator-approved plan and continued bonds and financial coverage
          | Keep Harbor licensed and operational longer |\n\n**State notice and approval**\n\nDo
          not search only for a rule called “license transfer.” Review each state
          for:\n\n- sale of substantially all assets;\n- change of control;\n- change
          in business plan;\n- change in licensed activities;\n- assignment of outstanding
          payment obligations;\n- change in responsible persons, locations, or agents;\n-
          license surrender or termination;\n- customer agreement assignment; and\n-
          movement of stored balances or customer funds.\n\nAn asset purchase might
          fall outside a technical “change of control” rule because Harbor’s ownership
          does not change. That does not resolve the issue. Harbor might still need
          a notice or surrender approval. Mosaic might separately need authority before
          it starts the regulated activity.\n\nThe state matrix should distinguish:\n\n-
          notice only;\n- approval before closing;\n- approval before customer migration;\n-
          new license required;\n- operation permitted while an application is pending;\n-
          regulator-approved transition available; and\n- no supported interim path.\n\n**Interim
          operation**\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed provider for a transition
          period. However, the structure must be real, not only contractual language.\n\nA
          supportable structure would normally need to show that:\n\n- Harbor remains
          responsible to customers.\n- Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.\n-
          Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.\n- Harbor’s licenses,
          bonds, and financial coverage remain active.\n- Customer funds and outstanding
          obligations remain covered.\n- Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints,
          and examinations.\n- Required records remain available.\n- Mosaic’s operational
          role is permitted.\n- The partner bank accepts the structure.\n- Each relevant
          regulator permits or accepts the structure.\n\nThe present plan creates
          tension with this approach. A single Mosaic account, one combined balance,
          and full access to Mosaic products make it harder to show that Harbor remains
          the true provider.\n\n**Partner-bank custody**\n\nA partner bank account
          is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter license. The key
          questions concern the complete activity and obligation flow.\n\nFor each
          customer balance and transfer, document:\n\n1. Who receives the customer’s
          instruction?\n2. Who accepts the obligation to transmit or return the funds?\n3.
          In whose name is the bank account held?\n4. Is it a custodial or “for benefit
          of” account?\n5. Who can direct withdrawals?\n6. Who owns the ledger and
          resolves errors?\n7. Who bears loss if a transfer fails?\n8. Which entity
          owes the customer a refund?\n9. Which entity’s license, bond, and permissible
          investments cover the obligation?\n10. Does the bank agreement permit assignment,
          migration, or a change in the program manager?\n11. Is bank consent required
          before closing or migration?\n12. What happens to funds if Harbor, Mosaic,
          or the bank relationship ends?\n\nA bank-led model might provide a different
          licensing analysis if the bank is the actual provider and Mosaic performs
          only permitted services. A bank account that merely holds funds for Mosaic
          or Harbor is different. The legal documents, customer terms, control rights,
          and actual operations must all support the claimed model.\n\nAlso review:\n\n-
          account segregation;\n- daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve
          funding;\n- bank setoff rights;\n- liens and security interests;\n- continuity
          if the account is frozen;\n- treatment of pending transfers;\n- return and
          chargeback duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n- customer disclosures; and\n-
          whether any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account
          structure.\n\n**Recommended closing position**\n\nKeep the acquisition closing
          separate from the regulated-service launch.\n\nFor the four Harbor-only
          states, use a state launch hold unless Mosaic has documented authority.
          For overlapping states, confirm that Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the
          complete post-close product set and funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s
          licenses or release its bonds until the applicable regulators permit it
          and all outstanding obligations have been assigned, completed, or placed
          into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis investigation does not change
          the current recommendation. It adds one material point: **partner-bank custody
          is part of the licensing analysis, but custody alone does not cure an authority
          gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch history: [Saved research 1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n</details>\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
          -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with missing
          underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's independent
          CIP/AML obligations\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe current plan for no re-verification
          is not yet supported. Mosaic’s compliance team has not confirmed whether
          Mosaic’s anti-money-laundering and customer identification program permits
          reliance on Harbor’s prior checks.\n\nMissing underlying documents prove
          a record gap. They do not by themselves prove that Harbor’s checks were
          invalid or that every affected user must be re-verified.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThis
          issue has not been researched. The applicable duties depend on Mosaic’s
          regulated status, its written program, the legal basis for any reliance,
          and the records that Mosaic must retain or access.\n\nThe saved record does
          not establish that Mosaic may satisfy its own duties using only Harbor’s
          pass/fail results.\n\n**Application**\n\nMosaic has pass/fail results for
          all Harbor users. It lacks underlying identity documents for users onboarded
          before 2023 because Harbor’s vendor closed in 2024.\n\nThe day-one plan
          would give migrated users a unified Mosaic account and full product access.
          If Mosaic’s program requires more evidence, the present data may not support
          unrestricted access for affected users.\n\nA proportionate response could
          include targeted re-verification, limits on affected accounts, or delayed
          access. The correct response depends on Mosaic’s program and the applicable
          legal requirements.\n\n**Next step**\n\nCompliance should document:\n\n-
          whether reliance on Harbor’s checks is permitted;\n- what evidence supports
          that reliance;\n- which records Mosaic must hold or be able to retrieve;\n-
          how many users lack required evidence;\n- whether risk-based remediation
          is allowed; and\n- what account limits apply until remediation is complete.\n\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:start -->\nInitial analysis
          — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:end
          -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38 -->\n### SAR and alert
          handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor's ~40 open alerts
          and SARs, and successor liability\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe approximately
          40 open alerts and recent suspicious activity report history should be reviewed
          through permitted diligence before Mosaic accepts unrestricted day-one operation.\n\nTheir
          unread status is a material information gap. It does not by itself prove
          a violation or establish that Mosaic inherits every Harbor obligation.\n\n**Rule
          and support**\n\nThis issue has not been researched. Responsibility may
          depend on which entity detected the activity, when any reporting deadline
          arose, whether Harbor remains in operation, the asset-purchase terms, and
          Mosaic’s post-close handling of the accounts.\n\nAccess to suspicious activity
          reports and related material must follow applicable confidentiality and
          access rules. Diligence should not be treated as an instruction to disclose
          or transfer restricted material to an unauthorized person.\n\n**Application**\n\nNo
          one has reviewed the alerts or the reported “handful” of suspicious activity
          reports from the last year. The record therefore does not show:\n\n- the
          age or type of each alert;\n- whether an investigation is complete;\n- whether
          a filing deadline is pending;\n- whether the same users will move to Mosaic;\n-
          whether any issue changes the deal risk; or\n- which entity will own each
          open case after close.\n\nMoving the accounts without resolving these points
          could separate active cases from the data, staff, and systems needed to
          complete them.\n\n**Next step**\n\nConduct a controlled review of the open
          cases and a permitted review of the filing history. Produce a case inventory
          that records status, deadlines, affected accounts, responsible entity, required
          records, and post-close ownership. Escalate any case that could affect migration
          eligibility or the transaction.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:start
          -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542
          -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
          when the SaaS contract terminates at close\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
          transaction feed should be tested and validated before migrated users receive
          full access. The saved record does not establish that repointing the feed
          on day one will prevent a monitoring gap.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThis
          issue has not been researched. The legal requirement depends on the anti-money-laundering
          duties that apply to the operating entity and on its risk-based monitoring
          program.\n\nOperational evidence is needed to show that transactions remain
          visible, complete, timely, and subject to the correct rules and case process.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s
          monitoring contract ends at close. Mosaic plans to repoint Harbor’s transaction
          feed to Mosaic’s engine on day one.\n\nThis creates a single transition
          point with no saved evidence of:\n\n- end-to-end testing;\n- transaction
          and field reconciliation;\n- rule coverage;\n- alert creation and routing;\n-
          handling of late or duplicate events;\n- retention of historical data;\n-
          ownership of cases across the cutoff; or\n- a rollback or temporary monitoring
          plan.\n\nThe open Harbor alerts make continuity more important because historical
          cases may depend on data from both systems.\n\n**Next step**\n\nComplete
          an end-to-end test and retain evidence of transaction completeness, rule
          execution, alert routing, reconciliation, historical-data access, case ownership,
          and fallback operation. If the test fails, restrict or delay activity that
          cannot be monitored.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:start
          -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
          -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
          money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
          proposed $50 bonus needs review before its planned close-plus-one launch.
          The present record does not contain enough information to determine the
          required terms or disclosures.\n\nThe bonus is not shown to be a deposit,
          interest payment, or prohibited offer merely because it provides $50.\n\n**Rule
          and support**\n\nThis issue has not been researched. The applicable rules
          depend on the actual offer, including eligibility, funding, transfer conditions,
          expiration, reversals, disclosures, and the states where it is offered.\n\nThe
          offer must also match the services Mosaic is authorized and operationally
          ready to provide.\n\n**Application**\n\nMarketing plans to offer $50 on
          a customer’s first transfer. The record does not state:\n\n- who qualifies;\n-
          who funds the payment;\n- the required transfer amount or type;\n- when
          the bonus becomes available;\n- whether it can be reversed;\n- whether users
          must remain active;\n- how limitations will be disclosed; or\n- whether
          the campaign will run in states subject to a launch hold.\n\nLaunching the
          offer before these points are settled could promise access or benefits that
          Mosaic cannot provide in an affected state.\n\n**Next step**\n\nObtain the
          complete offer terms, customer-facing copy, funding flow, eligibility rules,
          state scope, timing, reversal rules, and complaint process. Review them
          against the approved launch footprint and actual product availability.\n\n<!--
          retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66:start -->\nInitial analysis
          — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66:end
          -->\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n<!-- alternative:SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4
          -->\n### Bank-held funds timing test — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved
          alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
          this test only:\n\n- A bank would hold the relevant funds.\n- Mosaic would
          control transfer instructions.\n- The structure depends on completion of
          the bank contract and operating setup.\n- Migration would occur on November
          15, 2026.\n- Bank integration would be ready on December 3, 2026.\n- Pre-2023
          identity documents would remain missing.\n- Forty alert cases would remain
          pending.\n- Harbor’s monitoring service would end at close.\n\n**How it
          helps or hinders the objective**\n\nBank custody could change part of the
          funds-flow analysis. It does not establish that Mosaic can provide the regulated
          service.\n\nOn the test dates, this option makes the November 15 migration
          harder. December 3 readiness is 18 days after the hypothetical migration
          date.\n\n**Added risks**\n\nThe option adds contract, bank approval, technical
          integration, and operating-setup dependencies. Failure to complete them
          on time would prevent use of the tested structure for the November 15 date.\n\n**Issues
          left unresolved**\n\nThe option does not resolve the missing identity documents,
          pending alerts, monitoring transition, or the question of who is the actual
          regulated provider.\n\n**Next action**\n\nThe saved working note proposes
          that Mara Chen obtain a dated bank readiness plan and confirm whether the
          bank can support November 15. The plan should also assign resolution of
          the identity-record gap, 40 pending alerts, and replacement monitoring.
          This is proposed work, not an assigned action.\n\n<!-- alternative:SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6
          -->\n### Bank-held funds structure — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved
          alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
          this test only, a partner bank holds customer funds.\n\n**How it helps or
          hinders the objective**\n\nBank custody could support a different analysis
          if the bank is the actual provider and Mosaic performs only permitted services.
          Custody alone does not transfer Harbor’s licenses or remove Mosaic’s possible
          licensing duties.\n\n**Added risks**\n\nThe legal position would depend
          on customer contracts, control of transfer instructions, settlement, account
          titles, ledger control, repayment duties, bank consent, and actual operations.
          A structure that exists only in contract language would not resolve the
          operating-authority question.\n\n**Issues left unresolved**\n\nThis option
          leaves open:\n\n- who contracts with users;\n- who controls transfers and
          settlement;\n- who records balances and owes repayment;\n- how customer
          identification duties are allocated;\n- who monitors transactions;\n- who
          manages alerts and suspicious activity reports;\n- how privacy duties apply;
          and\n- which entity is responsible for the bonus campaign.\n\n**Next action**\n\nPrepare
          the proposed bank agreements, customer terms, funds-flow diagram, control
          model, and duty allocation. Then compare the actual structure with the licensing
          matrix. No owner or due date is recorded.\n\n## Next actions\n\nAll open
          actions below are proposed. No owner or due date has been assigned unless
          stated.\n\n1. **Review Harbor’s open alerts and permitted suspicious activity
          report history.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.
          \ \n   **Evidence needed:** Case inventory, age, status, deadlines, affected
          accounts, responsible entity, and migration effect.\n\n2. **Resolve the
          license footprint and authority for each affected state.**  \n   **Owner:**
          Not assigned. The saved licensing analysis proposes the licensing team and
          state regulatory counsel.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence
          needed:** Confirmed license lists, covered activities, operative state rules,
          filing receipts, approvals or non-objections, and any written regulator
          position.\n\n3. **Confirm whether Mosaic’s program permits reliance on Harbor’s
          prior customer checks.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned. Compliance confirmation
          is required.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Written
          program requirements, reliance basis, record requirements, affected-user
          count, and approved remediation or account limits.\n\n4. **Validate transaction-monitoring
          continuity.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.
          \ \n   **Evidence needed:** End-to-end test results, reconciliation, rule
          coverage, alert routing, historical-data access, case ownership, and fallback
          results.\n\n5. **Confirm the post-close service provider and funds flow.**
          \ \n   **Owner:** Not assigned. The saved licensing analysis proposes product
          and deal counsel.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:**
          Customer contracts, user interface, account titles, funds-flow diagram,
          control rights, repayment duties, bank agreement, and bank consent.\n\n6.
          **Review the complete $50 bonus proposal.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.
          \ \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Offer terms, copy,
          eligibility, funding, state scope, timing, reversals, disclosures, and complaint
          handling.\n\n7. **Confirm the operative closing date and year.**  \n   **Owner:**
          Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Current
          transaction timetable or executed deal document showing the close date.\n\nThe
          only recorded work item, [Orient to the request](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/work-items/WI-20260909-dc797b.md),
          is complete. It was owned by Lawyer and had no due date.\n\n## Current work
          product and supporting records\n\n- No current draft or final work-product
          path is saved.\n- [Known facts](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md)\n-
          [Original request](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/request.md)\n- [Licensing
          research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
          [Prior dossier revision](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier-revisions/DOS-a339a10414a6329eff9f.md)\n\n[Open
          saved dossier revision](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier-revisions/DOS-dc2adc8aaff5906e6734.md)\n\nDossier
          generated and saved."

        captured_record:
          message_id: MSG-20260912-25f507
          role: assistant
          content: "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe Harbor
            Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned Nov
            15 close. This is the accepted working view. It is not a recorded decision.\n\nMosaic
            Relay plans an asset purchase. It then plans to move 240,000 consumer
            users and 12,000 business accounts into a unified Mosaic account on day
            one after close. Users would receive full access to Mosaic products.\n\nThe
            main obstacle is whether Mosaic has authority to provide each post-close
            service in every affected state. Mosaic should not assume that Harbor’s
            money transmitter licenses transfer with the purchased assets.\n\nThe
            other material obstacles are:\n\n- Mosaic has not confirmed whether its
            anti-money-laundering and customer identification program permits reliance
            on Harbor’s prior know-your-customer results.\n- Underlying identity documents
            are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor’s approximately
            40 open alerts and recent suspicious activity report history have not
            been reviewed.\n- Harbor’s monitoring service ends at close. The replacement
            feed has not been validated.\n- The terms and operating structure of the
            planned $50 welcome bonus are unknown.\n\nThe full day-one migration remains
            the planning baseline. State launch holds, account restrictions, or delayed
            product access remain possible safeguards if the open conditions are not
            resolved. No decisions are recorded.\n\n### Assumptions used\n\n- Harbor
            is a licensed money transmitter subject to applicable state and federal
            anti-money-laundering requirements. This assumption affects the licensing,
            customer identification, alert, and monitoring analysis.\n- Mosaic will
            become the operating provider immediately after close. This affects whether
            Harbor can remain the licensed provider during a transition.\n- The analysis
            does not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that its prior identity
            checks satisfy Mosaic’s requirements, or that monitoring can continue
            without a gap.\n- Mosaic’s reported 41-state license footprint is treated
            as a reported fact.\n- The acquisition structure is no longer assumed
            to be unknown. The reported structure is an asset purchase.\n\n### Record
            conflicts\n\n- Mosaic reportedly has licenses in 41 states, and the combined
            footprint is 44 states. `44 − 41 = 3`, but the record says the acquisition
            opens four new markets. This affects which jurisdictions require new authority
            or launch restrictions. The license lists and the intended meaning of
            “market” are needed.\n- Matter metadata gives a target date of `2026-09-11`.
            The reported close is “Nov 15,” approximately ten weeks after the Sept.
            9 intake. A saved hypothetical uses November 15, 2026, but that does not
            establish the actual closing year. The operative close date and year remain
            unresolved.\n\n## Decision question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor Pay
            acquisition migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n##
            Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045 -->\n### Money transmission
            licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state
            footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n\n**Current
            answer**\n\nMosaic should not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses
            as assets that automatically move to Mosaic in the asset purchase.\n\nThe
            acquisition may close separately from the service launch. Mosaic should
            not start regulated services in a state unless it has documented authority
            for the complete post-close activity.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe saved
            research concludes that the answer must be determined state by state.
            Review must cover Mosaic’s operating authority, transaction notices and
            approvals, interim operation, outstanding obligations, and Harbor’s license
            surrender.\n\nFour sources were retrieved, but no relevant passages were
            read or verified. They do not establish an operative state rule:\n\n-
            [Research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
            [CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — retrieved, but relevant passage
            not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538-157583424427.md)\n-
            [New York Department of Financial Services licensing page — retrieved,
            but relevant passage not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fa80c95c5393.md)\n\nThe
            model act is not proof of the law in any specific state.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor
            reportedly has licenses in 38 states. Mosaic reportedly has licenses in
            41 states. Their combined footprint is reported as 44 states. Mosaic currently
            plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in the new markets.\n\nThe unified
            Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products suggest
            that Mosaic may become the actual service provider. If so, keeping Harbor’s
            entity or licenses active might not give Mosaic authority.\n\nA transition
            in which Harbor remains the licensed provider is possible only if the
            customer contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses, bonds, records,
            and applicable state rules support that result.\n\nA partner bank holding
            funds would not, by itself, establish Mosaic’s authority. The answer depends
            on who contracts with users, controls transfers, owes repayment, maintains
            balances, resolves errors, and carries the regulated duties.\n\n**Next
            step**\n\nIdentify the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare one state
            matrix covering:\n\n- Mosaic’s authority for each post-close activity;\n-
            notices, filings, approvals, and deadlines;\n- operation while an application
            is pending;\n- transfer of customer agreements and outstanding obligations;\n-
            bank custody and control;\n- Harbor’s run-off duties, bonds, and license
            surrender; and\n- the launch restriction needed if authority is not established.\n\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved
            research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nDo not rely on transferability
            without an applicable state rule, approval, or written regulator position.\n\nThe
            answer must be determined state by state and must cover more than technical
            change-of-control rules.\n\nThis path is possible only if Harbor remains
            the real provider and the relevant states permit the arrangement. The
            unified Mosaic account design may conflict with that position.\n\nThe
            result depends on the contracts and actual funds flow. Custody alone should
            not be treated as a licensing exemption or transfer mechanism.\n\nResearch
            saved. 4 sources retrieved; 0 with passages read.\n\nNext step: Identify
            the four Harbor-only states and complete one matrix covering license authority,
            transaction filings, interim operation, bank custody, outstanding obligations,
            and license surrender.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Detailed analysis</summary>\n\n**Practical
            answer**\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets
            that move to Mosaic in the asset purchase.** Use this closing rule:\n\n>
            **No confirmed authority means no regulated launch by Mosaic in that state.**\n\nThe
            asset purchase can still close. However, Mosaic should not activate regulated
            services in the four Harbor-only states unless one of these conditions
            is met:\n\n1. Mosaic obtains its own license.\n2. The state approves a
            transfer or other license change.\n3. The regulator confirms a lawful
            interim structure.\n4. Harbor remains the real licensed provider under
            a valid transition plan.\n5. Mosaic blocks regulated functions in that
            state.\n\nThe planned unified Mosaic account is important. It suggests
            that Mosaic, not Harbor, will become the service provider. If that is
            correct, keeping Harbor’s legal entity and licenses alive might not give
            Mosaic authority to operate.\n\n**No verified operative authority retrieved.**
            The collection found the CSBS Model Money Transmission Modernization Act
            and a New York regulator licensing page. However, no exact provision about
            an asset sale, license transfer, interim operation, or custody was available
            for review. Also, a model act is not proof of the law adopted in a specific
            state. The state-specific conclusions below remain conditional.\n\n**Work
            needed before launch**\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by |
            Evidence to proceed | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Identify
            the four Harbor-only states | These states have the clearest authority
            gap | Licensing team | Now | Confirmed license list and covered activities
            | Block regulated functions in those states |\n| Build a matrix for every
            affected state | Transfer, notice, approval, and surrender rules can differ
            | State regulatory counsel | Before the closing conditions are final |
            Applicable rule, filing deadline, regulator response, and license status
            | Delay migration in the affected state |\n| Confirm the post-close service
            provider | The licensed entity must match the actual operating model |
            Product and deal counsel | Before customer notices and account design
            are final | Contracts, user interface, funds-flow diagram, and operating
            roles | Keep Harbor as the actual provider where permitted |\n| Review
            notices and approvals | An asset sale can create separate seller and buyer
            requirements | Licensing team | Before each state deadline | Filing receipts
            and required approvals or non-objections | Make approval a state launch
            condition |\n| Confirm interim operating authority | A pending application
            should not be assumed to permit operation | State regulatory counsel |
            Before close | Applicable rule or written regulator confirmation | Keep
            Harbor customers segregated or restrict transactions |\n| Review partner-bank
            arrangements | Bank custody does not, by itself, establish Mosaic’s licensing
            position | Payments counsel and bank relationship owner | Before balances
            move | Bank agreements, account titles, control rights, reconciliation
            design, and bank consent | Keep funds and obligations in the existing
            structure |\n| Prepare license run-off and surrender plans | Harbor may
            retain duties for balances, claims, records, and reports | Harbor compliance
            and deal counsel | Before surrender or operational shutdown | Regulator-approved
            plan and continued bonds and financial coverage | Keep Harbor licensed
            and operational longer |\n\n**State notice and approval**\n\nDo not search
            only for a rule called “license transfer.” Review each state for:\n\n-
            sale of substantially all assets;\n- change of control;\n- change in business
            plan;\n- change in licensed activities;\n- assignment of outstanding payment
            obligations;\n- change in responsible persons, locations, or agents;\n-
            license surrender or termination;\n- customer agreement assignment; and\n-
            movement of stored balances or customer funds.\n\nAn asset purchase might
            fall outside a technical “change of control” rule because Harbor’s ownership
            does not change. That does not resolve the issue. Harbor might still need
            a notice or surrender approval. Mosaic might separately need authority
            before it starts the regulated activity.\n\nThe state matrix should distinguish:\n\n-
            notice only;\n- approval before closing;\n- approval before customer migration;\n-
            new license required;\n- operation permitted while an application is pending;\n-
            regulator-approved transition available; and\n- no supported interim path.\n\n**Interim
            operation**\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed provider for a transition
            period. However, the structure must be real, not only contractual language.\n\nA
            supportable structure would normally need to show that:\n\n- Harbor remains
            responsible to customers.\n- Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.\n-
            Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.\n- Harbor’s licenses,
            bonds, and financial coverage remain active.\n- Customer funds and outstanding
            obligations remain covered.\n- Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints,
            and examinations.\n- Required records remain available.\n- Mosaic’s operational
            role is permitted.\n- The partner bank accepts the structure.\n- Each
            relevant regulator permits or accepts the structure.\n\nThe present plan
            creates tension with this approach. A single Mosaic account, one combined
            balance, and full access to Mosaic products make it harder to show that
            Harbor remains the true provider.\n\n**Partner-bank custody**\n\nA partner
            bank account is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter
            license. The key questions concern the complete activity and obligation
            flow.\n\nFor each customer balance and transfer, document:\n\n1. Who receives
            the customer’s instruction?\n2. Who accepts the obligation to transmit
            or return the funds?\n3. In whose name is the bank account held?\n4. Is
            it a custodial or “for benefit of” account?\n5. Who can direct withdrawals?\n6.
            Who owns the ledger and resolves errors?\n7. Who bears loss if a transfer
            fails?\n8. Which entity owes the customer a refund?\n9. Which entity’s
            license, bond, and permissible investments cover the obligation?\n10.
            Does the bank agreement permit assignment, migration, or a change in the
            program manager?\n11. Is bank consent required before closing or migration?\n12.
            What happens to funds if Harbor, Mosaic, or the bank relationship ends?\n\nA
            bank-led model might provide a different licensing analysis if the bank
            is the actual provider and Mosaic performs only permitted services. A
            bank account that merely holds funds for Mosaic or Harbor is different.
            The legal documents, customer terms, control rights, and actual operations
            must all support the claimed model.\n\nAlso review:\n\n- account segregation;\n-
            daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve funding;\n- bank setoff
            rights;\n- liens and security interests;\n- continuity if the account
            is frozen;\n- treatment of pending transfers;\n- return and chargeback
            duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n- customer disclosures; and\n- whether
            any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account structure.\n\n**Recommended
            closing position**\n\nKeep the acquisition closing separate from the regulated-service
            launch.\n\nFor the four Harbor-only states, use a state launch hold unless
            Mosaic has documented authority. For overlapping states, confirm that
            Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the complete post-close product set and
            funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s licenses or release its bonds
            until the applicable regulators permit it and all outstanding obligations
            have been assigned, completed, or placed into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis
            investigation does not change the current recommendation. It adds one
            material point: **partner-bank custody is part of the licensing analysis,
            but custody alone does not cure an authority gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch
            history: [Saved research 1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n</details>\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
            -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with
            missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's
            independent CIP/AML obligations\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe current plan
            for no re-verification is not yet supported. Mosaic’s compliance team
            has not confirmed whether Mosaic’s anti-money-laundering and customer
            identification program permits reliance on Harbor’s prior checks.\n\nMissing
            underlying documents prove a record gap. They do not by themselves prove
            that Harbor’s checks were invalid or that every affected user must be
            re-verified.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThis issue has not been researched.
            The applicable duties depend on Mosaic’s regulated status, its written
            program, the legal basis for any reliance, and the records that Mosaic
            must retain or access.\n\nThe saved record does not establish that Mosaic
            may satisfy its own duties using only Harbor’s pass/fail results.\n\n**Application**\n\nMosaic
            has pass/fail results for all Harbor users. It lacks underlying identity
            documents for users onboarded before 2023 because Harbor’s vendor closed
            in 2024.\n\nThe day-one plan would give migrated users a unified Mosaic
            account and full product access. If Mosaic’s program requires more evidence,
            the present data may not support unrestricted access for affected users.\n\nA
            proportionate response could include targeted re-verification, limits
            on affected accounts, or delayed access. The correct response depends
            on Mosaic’s program and the applicable legal requirements.\n\n**Next step**\n\nCompliance
            should document:\n\n- whether reliance on Harbor’s checks is permitted;\n-
            what evidence supports that reliance;\n- which records Mosaic must hold
            or be able to retrieve;\n- how many users lack required evidence;\n- whether
            risk-based remediation is allowed; and\n- what account limits apply until
            remediation is complete.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:start
            -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38
            -->\n### SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
            Harbor's ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n\n**Current
            answer**\n\nThe approximately 40 open alerts and recent suspicious activity
            report history should be reviewed through permitted diligence before Mosaic
            accepts unrestricted day-one operation.\n\nTheir unread status is a material
            information gap. It does not by itself prove a violation or establish
            that Mosaic inherits every Harbor obligation.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThis
            issue has not been researched. Responsibility may depend on which entity
            detected the activity, when any reporting deadline arose, whether Harbor
            remains in operation, the asset-purchase terms, and Mosaic’s post-close
            handling of the accounts.\n\nAccess to suspicious activity reports and
            related material must follow applicable confidentiality and access rules.
            Diligence should not be treated as an instruction to disclose or transfer
            restricted material to an unauthorized person.\n\n**Application**\n\nNo
            one has reviewed the alerts or the reported “handful” of suspicious activity
            reports from the last year. The record therefore does not show:\n\n- the
            age or type of each alert;\n- whether an investigation is complete;\n-
            whether a filing deadline is pending;\n- whether the same users will move
            to Mosaic;\n- whether any issue changes the deal risk; or\n- which entity
            will own each open case after close.\n\nMoving the accounts without resolving
            these points could separate active cases from the data, staff, and systems
            needed to complete them.\n\n**Next step**\n\nConduct a controlled review
            of the open cases and a permitted review of the filing history. Produce
            a case inventory that records status, deadlines, affected accounts, responsible
            entity, required records, and post-close ownership. Escalate any case
            that could affect migration eligibility or the transaction.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:start
            -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542
            -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
            when the SaaS contract terminates at close\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
            transaction feed should be tested and validated before migrated users
            receive full access. The saved record does not establish that repointing
            the feed on day one will prevent a monitoring gap.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThis
            issue has not been researched. The legal requirement depends on the anti-money-laundering
            duties that apply to the operating entity and on its risk-based monitoring
            program.\n\nOperational evidence is needed to show that transactions remain
            visible, complete, timely, and subject to the correct rules and case process.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s
            monitoring contract ends at close. Mosaic plans to repoint Harbor’s transaction
            feed to Mosaic’s engine on day one.\n\nThis creates a single transition
            point with no saved evidence of:\n\n- end-to-end testing;\n- transaction
            and field reconciliation;\n- rule coverage;\n- alert creation and routing;\n-
            handling of late or duplicate events;\n- retention of historical data;\n-
            ownership of cases across the cutoff; or\n- a rollback or temporary monitoring
            plan.\n\nThe open Harbor alerts make continuity more important because
            historical cases may depend on data from both systems.\n\n**Next step**\n\nComplete
            an end-to-end test and retain evidence of transaction completeness, rule
            execution, alert routing, reconciliation, historical-data access, case
            ownership, and fallback operation. If the test fails, restrict or delay
            activity that cannot be monitored.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:start
            -->\nInitial analysis — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
            -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
            money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
            proposed $50 bonus needs review before its planned close-plus-one launch.
            The present record does not contain enough information to determine the
            required terms or disclosures.\n\nThe bonus is not shown to be a deposit,
            interest payment, or prohibited offer merely because it provides $50.\n\n**Rule
            and support**\n\nThis issue has not been researched. The applicable rules
            depend on the actual offer, including eligibility, funding, transfer conditions,
            expiration, reversals, disclosures, and the states where it is offered.\n\nThe
            offer must also match the services Mosaic is authorized and operationally
            ready to provide.\n\n**Application**\n\nMarketing plans to offer $50 on
            a customer’s first transfer. The record does not state:\n\n- who qualifies;\n-
            who funds the payment;\n- the required transfer amount or type;\n- when
            the bonus becomes available;\n- whether it can be reversed;\n- whether
            users must remain active;\n- how limitations will be disclosed; or\n-
            whether the campaign will run in states subject to a launch hold.\n\nLaunching
            the offer before these points are settled could promise access or benefits
            that Mosaic cannot provide in an affected state.\n\n**Next step**\n\nObtain
            the complete offer terms, customer-facing copy, funding flow, eligibility
            rules, state scope, timing, reversal rules, and complaint process. Review
            them against the approved launch footprint and actual product availability.\n\n<!--
            retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66:start -->\nInitial analysis
            — no completed research is saved for this issue.\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66:end
            -->\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n<!-- alternative:SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4
            -->\n### Bank-held funds timing test — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved
            alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-0f23edfc89ec6ecaf60a13e4.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
            this test only:\n\n- A bank would hold the relevant funds.\n- Mosaic would
            control transfer instructions.\n- The structure depends on completion
            of the bank contract and operating setup.\n- Migration would occur on
            November 15, 2026.\n- Bank integration would be ready on December 3, 2026.\n-
            Pre-2023 identity documents would remain missing.\n- Forty alert cases
            would remain pending.\n- Harbor’s monitoring service would end at close.\n\n**How
            it helps or hinders the objective**\n\nBank custody could change part
            of the funds-flow analysis. It does not establish that Mosaic can provide
            the regulated service.\n\nOn the test dates, this option makes the November
            15 migration harder. December 3 readiness is 18 days after the hypothetical
            migration date.\n\n**Added risks**\n\nThe option adds contract, bank approval,
            technical integration, and operating-setup dependencies. Failure to complete
            them on time would prevent use of the tested structure for the November
            15 date.\n\n**Issues left unresolved**\n\nThe option does not resolve
            the missing identity documents, pending alerts, monitoring transition,
            or the question of who is the actual regulated provider.\n\n**Next action**\n\nThe
            saved working note proposes that Mara Chen obtain a dated bank readiness
            plan and confirm whether the bank can support November 15. The plan should
            also assign resolution of the identity-record gap, 40 pending alerts,
            and replacement monitoring. This is proposed work, not an assigned action.\n\n<!--
            alternative:SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6 -->\n### Bank-held funds structure
            — **Hypothetical — not adopted**\n\n[Saved alternative](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/scenarios/SCN-406906c91ab0aba4313b54a6.md)\n\n**Assumptions**\n\nFor
            this test only, a partner bank holds customer funds.\n\n**How it helps
            or hinders the objective**\n\nBank custody could support a different analysis
            if the bank is the actual provider and Mosaic performs only permitted
            services. Custody alone does not transfer Harbor’s licenses or remove
            Mosaic’s possible licensing duties.\n\n**Added risks**\n\nThe legal position
            would depend on customer contracts, control of transfer instructions,
            settlement, account titles, ledger control, repayment duties, bank consent,
            and actual operations. A structure that exists only in contract language
            would not resolve the operating-authority question.\n\n**Issues left unresolved**\n\nThis
            option leaves open:\n\n- who contracts with users;\n- who controls transfers
            and settlement;\n- who records balances and owes repayment;\n- how customer
            identification duties are allocated;\n- who monitors transactions;\n-
            who manages alerts and suspicious activity reports;\n- how privacy duties
            apply; and\n- which entity is responsible for the bonus campaign.\n\n**Next
            action**\n\nPrepare the proposed bank agreements, customer terms, funds-flow
            diagram, control model, and duty allocation. Then compare the actual structure
            with the licensing matrix. No owner or due date is recorded.\n\n## Next
            actions\n\nAll open actions below are proposed. No owner or due date has
            been assigned unless stated.\n\n1. **Review Harbor’s open alerts and permitted
            suspicious activity report history.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n
            \  **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Case inventory,
            age, status, deadlines, affected accounts, responsible entity, and migration
            effect.\n\n2. **Resolve the license footprint and authority for each affected
            state.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned. The saved licensing analysis proposes
            the licensing team and state regulatory counsel.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.
            \ \n   **Evidence needed:** Confirmed license lists, covered activities,
            operative state rules, filing receipts, approvals or non-objections, and
            any written regulator position.\n\n3. **Confirm whether Mosaic’s program
            permits reliance on Harbor’s prior customer checks.**  \n   **Owner:**
            Not assigned. Compliance confirmation is required.  \n   **Date:** Not
            assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Written program requirements, reliance
            basis, record requirements, affected-user count, and approved remediation
            or account limits.\n\n4. **Validate transaction-monitoring continuity.**
            \ \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence
            needed:** End-to-end test results, reconciliation, rule coverage, alert
            routing, historical-data access, case ownership, and fallback results.\n\n5.
            **Confirm the post-close service provider and funds flow.**  \n   **Owner:**
            Not assigned. The saved licensing analysis proposes product and deal counsel.
            \ \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Customer contracts,
            user interface, account titles, funds-flow diagram, control rights, repayment
            duties, bank agreement, and bank consent.\n\n6. **Review the complete
            $50 bonus proposal.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** Not
            assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Offer terms, copy, eligibility, funding,
            state scope, timing, reversals, disclosures, and complaint handling.\n\n7.
            **Confirm the operative closing date and year.**  \n   **Owner:** Not
            assigned.  \n   **Date:** Not assigned.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Current
            transaction timetable or executed deal document showing the close date.\n\nThe
            only recorded work item, [Orient to the request](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/work-items/WI-20260909-dc797b.md),
            is complete. It was owned by Lawyer and had no due date.\n\n## Current
            work product and supporting records\n\n- No current draft or final work-product
            path is saved.\n- [Known facts](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md)\n-
            [Original request](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/request.md)\n- [Licensing
            research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
            [Prior dossier revision](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier-revisions/DOS-a339a10414a6329eff9f.md)\n\n[Open
            saved dossier revision](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier-revisions/DOS-dc2adc8aaff5906e6734.md)\n\nDossier
            generated and saved."
