                  - start: 0
                    end: 3962
                    text: '# Known Facts


                      - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                      (~10 weeks out).

                      - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                      into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                      account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                      - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                      by Harbor.

                      - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                      Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                      four new markets.

                      - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
                      Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
                      documents for users onboarded before 2023.

                      - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                      contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                      feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                      - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
                      first transfer, launching close+1.

                      - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                      from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                      - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                      into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                      account and balance.

                      - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                      users were already KYC''d.

                      - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
                      pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying documents
                      are missing for users onboarded before 2023.

                      - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                      contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                      feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                      - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                      from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                      - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                      (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                      - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                      on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
                      or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with
                      compliance

                      - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs
                      from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                      - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint,
                      does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                      or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                      - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                      what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                      identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                      known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                      on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                      - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the
                      last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open
                      alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in
                      diligence.

                      - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                      what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                      before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently
                      plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                      ## Assumptions


                      - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                      and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                      the acquisition without new state approval

                      - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                      Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the
                      underlying documents

                      - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                      and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                      - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                      to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                      confirmed).

                      - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                      in 41 states (per the request).

                      - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or
                      stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and
                      SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                      '
                  source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                    path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md
                    text: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
                      or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                      certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant
                      that is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner].
                      If the certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner]
                      may order the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner]
                      may find necessary to enable the independent or certified public
                      accountant or \nindependent public accountant to remove the
                      qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
                      \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates
                      within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner]
                      is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission
                      of the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that
                      such \nfunctionality is consistent with the requirements of
                      this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report
                      shall include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1)
                      \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification
                      number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical
                      address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted
                      in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8)
                      \nContact person name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart
                      date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting
                      as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court
                      orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information
                      the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect to the
                      authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21
                      \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to implement state
                      use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR)
                      process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS
                      to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops
                      new functionality to prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"
                  - &id121
                    unit_id: p000028

                    text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
                      within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know
                      of the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe
                      filing of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited
                      States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended
                      or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization;
                      \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee
                      for \nreceivership, the commencement of any other judicial or
                      administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or reorganization,
                      or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of its
                      \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to
                      revoke or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country in which
                      the licensee engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee
                      shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within three business
                      \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
                      of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction
                      of the licensee or of a key individual \nor person in control
                      of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction
                      of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank
                      Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized delegate
                      shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
                      record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements
                      as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and
                      state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing
                      of \na complete and accurate report required under this [Section
                      7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant
                      with the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06
                      Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following records,
                      for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least
                      [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission
                      obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least
                      monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income,
                      and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
                      records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"

                    text: "29 \n \n(5) \nrecords of each outstanding money transmission
                      obligation \npaid within the [three]-year period; \n(6) \na
                      list of the last known names and addresses of all of the \nlicensee's
                      authorized delegates; and \n(7) \nany other records the [Commissioner]
                      reasonably requires \nby rule. \n(b) \nThe items specified in
                      [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained in any form of \nrecord.
                      \n(c) \nRecords specified in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained
                      outside this state \nif they are made accessible to the [Commissioner]
                      on [seven] business-days' notice that is sent in \na record.
                      \n(d) \nAll records maintained by the licensee as required in
                      [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to inspection by the [Commissioner]
                      pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)]. \n \nARTICLE VIII \nAuthorized
                      Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship Between Licensee and Authorized
                      Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section 8.01], \"remit\" means to
                      make direct payments of money to \na licensee or its representative
                      authorized to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in
                      an \naccount specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee
                      is authorized to conduct business through an authorized \ndelegate
                      or allows a person to act as the licensee's authorized delegate,
                      the licensee must: \n(1) \nadopt, and update as necessary, written
                      policies and procedures \nreasonably designed to ensure that
                      the licensee's authorized delegates comply with \napplicable
                      state and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written contract
                      that complies with [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct
                      a reasonable risk-based background investigation sufficient
                      \nfor the licensee to determine whether the authorized delegate
                      has complied and will likely \ncomply with applicable state
                      and federal law. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate must operate
                      in full compliance with this [Act]. \n(d) \nThe written contract
                      required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed by the \nlicensee
                      and the authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"

                    text: "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed
                      by a licensee, provided that \nconfidential information, including,
                      but not limited to, prices and fees for such bond is \nredacted;
                      \n(5) \nCopies of any non-confidential final orders of the [Department]
                      \nrelating to any violation of this [Act] or regulations implementing
                      this [Act]; and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine
                      or penalty under this [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a)
                      \nThe [Commissioner] may conduct an examination or investigation
                      of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate or otherwise take independent
                      action authorized by this [Act] or by \na rule adopted or order
                      issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary or appropriate
                      to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing
                      this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy
                      Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may: \n(1)
                      \nconduct an examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner]
                      may reasonably require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction
                      with an examination \nconducted by representatives of other
                      state agencies or agencies of another state or of the \nfederal
                      government; \n(3) \n  accept the examination report of another
                      state agency or an agency \nof another state or of the federal
                      government, or a report prepared by an independent \naccounting
                      firm, which on being accepted is considered for all purposes
                      as an official report \nof the [Commissioner]; and \n(4) \nsummon
                      and examine under oath a key individual or employee of a \nlicensee
                      or authorized delegate and require the person to produce records
                      regarding any \nmatter related to the condition and business
                      of the licensee or authorized delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or
                      authorized delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner] \nshall
                      have full and complete access to, all records the [Commissioner]
                      may reasonably require to \nconduct a complete examination.
                      The records must be provided at the location and in the format
                      \nspecified by the [Commissioner], provided, the [Commissioner]
                      may utilize multistate record \nproduction standards and examination
                      procedures when such standards will reasonably achieve \nthe
                      requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless otherwise
                      directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee shall pay all \ncosts
                      reasonably incurred in connection with an examination of the
                      licensee or the licensee's \n \n8 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
                      is encouraged to instruct examiners to: (1) include all examination
                      requests in \nthe Day 1 letter that may require the licensee
                      to obtain records located outside of the U.S., including but
                      not limited \nto evidence demonstrating when an outstanding
                      money transmission obligation has been extinguished; and (2)
                      accept \nelectronic bank statements as provided to the licensee
                      by the bank.\n"

              title: issues.md
              support_state: supplied
              source_type: workspace
              available_excerpt: '# Issues and workstreams


                - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
                the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
                the acquisition

                - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
                underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s
                independent CIP/AML obligations

                - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                money transmission or consumer protection implications

                - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                -->

                '

            - source_id: SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c
              source_hash: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
              source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
              original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md
              title: facts.md
              support_state: supplied
              source_type: workspace
              available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


                - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                Harbor.

                - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.

                - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC''d.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay''s engine on day 1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
                buys Harbor''s assets)

                - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC;
                compliance must confirm.

                - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
                been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR
                history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                ## Assumptions


                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
                acquisition without new state approval

                - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                documents

                - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                in 41 states (per the request).

                - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations
                transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                '

              available_excerpt: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall
                include or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant that
                is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the
                certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order
                the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
                to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent
                public accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized
                Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of
                authorized delegates within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20
                The [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS
                for the submission of the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)]
                provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the requirements
                of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall
                include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany
                legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3)
                \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing
                address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny
                fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number,
                and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10)
                \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;
                \ \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny
                other information the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect
                to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21
                \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to implement state use
                of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21
                Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section
                7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to
                prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"

                an agency \nof another state or of the federal government, or a report
                prepared by an independent \naccounting firm, which on being accepted
                is considered for all purposes as an official report \nof the [Commissioner];
                and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under oath a key individual or employee
                of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate and require the person to produce
                records regarding any \nmatter related to the condition and business
                of the licensee or authorized delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized
                delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner] \nshall have full and
                complete access to, all records the [Commissioner] may reasonably
                require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records must be provided
                at the location and in the format \nspecified by the [Commissioner],

                achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless

                demonstrating when an outstanding money transmission obligation has
                been extinguished; and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as
                provided to the licensee by the bank.\n"

            title: 'Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring vendor transition:
              continuity'
            question: 'Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring vendor transition:
              continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract terminates
              at close. Harbor''s monitoring contract ends at close. A failed or untested
              change could create an immediate gap in detection, records, and case
              handling.

              Lawyer''s accepted priorities (private matter context):

              Make KYC, alert resolution, and monitoring continuity formal close and
              migration gates.: These linked controls affect the full migrated population
              and can create immediate exposure that is difficult to repair later.

              inputs:
                business_question:
                  question_id: BQ-c9d7c39f6380eb60
                  text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need
                    legal review before the Nov 15 close?
                  revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
                facts:
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
                  text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                    (~10 weeks out).
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
                  text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
                  text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd
                    by Harbor.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
                  text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                    four new markets.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
                  text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
                    Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
                    documents for users onboarded before 2023.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
                  text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction
                    feed at Mosaic's engine on day 1.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
                  text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                    transfer, launching close+1.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
                  text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
                  source_ids:
                  - REQ-20260909-283892
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
                  text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-9835ba
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
                  text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor
                    users were already KYC'd.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-9835ba
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
                  text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
                    pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying documents
                    are missing for users onboarded before 2023.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-9835ba
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
                  text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                    feed to Mosaic Relay's engine on day 1.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-9835ba
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
                  text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-9835ba
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
                  text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                    (Mosaic buys Harbor's assets)
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
                  text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                    on another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or
                    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
                  text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs
                    from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
                  text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint,
                    does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses
                    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
                  text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer
                    identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                    known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance
                    on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
                  text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the
                    last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open
                    alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
                  text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                    what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                    to use or assume Harbor's licenses for the four new markets.
                  source_ids:
                  - MSG-20260909-2e549e
                  origin: null
                  verification_status: null
                assumptions:
                - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-29b823
                  text: Mosaic Relay's existing money transmission licenses and Harbor's
                    MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
                    without new state approval
                  reason: Needed to continue
                - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-3c5756
                  text: The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
                    Relay's own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                    documents
                  reason: Needed to continue
                - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-1a519f
                  text: The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
                    before close without a monitoring gap
                  reason: Needed to continue
                - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-ca7dfd
                  text: Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
                    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).
                  reason: Needed to continue
                - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-d40239
                  text: Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41

                  - start: 0
                    end: 817
                    text: '# Issues and workstreams


                      - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                      under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s
                      MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition

                      - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                      missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                      Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                      - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                      Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                      - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                      when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                      - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any
                      state money transmission or consumer protection implications

                      - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!--
                      issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06 -->

                      '
                  source_version: bfa5205c5c55347ff2e44736fdf58a3f8fade088059bc29b892ac7fa1e500afb
                source:SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c:
                  kind: source
                  record_id: SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
                  revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
                  file_revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                  passages: &id125
                  - start: 0
                    end: 3962
                    text: '# Known Facts


                      - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                      (~10 weeks out).

                      - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                      into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                      account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                      - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                      by Harbor.

                      - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                      Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                      four new markets.

                      - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
                      Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
                      documents for users onboarded before 2023.

                      - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                      contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                      feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                      - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
                      first transfer, launching close+1.

                      - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                      from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                      - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                      into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                      account and balance.

                      - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                      users were already KYC''d.

                      - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
                      pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying documents
                      are missing for users onboarded before 2023.

                      - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                      contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                      feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                      - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                      from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                      - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                      (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                      - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                      on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
                      or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with
                      compliance

                      - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs
                      from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                      - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint,
                      does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                      or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                      - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                      what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                      identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                      known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                      on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                      - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the
                      last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open
                      alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in
                      diligence.

                      - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                      what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                      before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently
                      plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                      ## Assumptions


                      - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                      and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                      the acquisition without new state approval

                      - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                      Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the
                      underlying documents

                      - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                      and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                      - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                      to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                      confirmed).

                      - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                      in 41 states (per the request).

                      - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or
                      stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and
                      SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                      '
                  source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                  - start: 0
                    end: 6000
                    text: '# Harbor 2 matter dossier


                      ## Current position


                      The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before
                      the planned Nov 15 close. This is the accepted working view.
                      No decision has been recorded.


                      This draft recommends continuing close preparation but making
                      the day-one service migration conditional. Mosaic should not
                      give all Harbor users full access until:


                      1. Mosaic has documented authority for each post-close service
                      in each affected state.

                      2. Compliance confirms that Mosaic may rely on Harbor’s know-your-customer
                      (KYC) results, or defines and completes remediation.

                      3. Authorized reviewers assess Harbor’s open alerts and suspicious
                      activity report (SAR) history.

                      4. Mosaic tests the replacement transaction-monitoring feed
                      and finds no material coverage gap.


                      If a condition is not met, Mosaic should hold the affected state
                      launch, restrict affected accounts, or delay full product access.
                      The $50 welcome bonus should also wait for review of its structure,
                      terms, funding, and disclosures.


                      The saved material does not establish that the acquisition close
                      itself must wait. However, the unread alerts and SAR history
                      could affect deal terms, risk allocation, or the decision to
                      close.


                      ### Assumptions used


                      - Harbor is subject to the state money-transmission and federal
                      anti-money-laundering requirements discussed below. The licensing,
                      KYC, alert, and monitoring conclusions depend on this unverified
                      legal premise.

                      - Mosaic will become the operating provider when Harbor users
                      receive a unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access
                      to Mosaic products. The licensing analysis depends on this inference.

                      - The analysis does not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer,
                      that Harbor’s KYC results satisfy Mosaic’s program, or that
                      the monitoring transition will work without a gap.


                      ### Record conflicts


                      - Harbor reportedly has licenses in 38 states, Mosaic has licenses
                      in 41 states, and the combined footprint is 44 states. A 44-state
                      footprint is three states larger than Mosaic’s 41-state footprint,
                      but the record says the acquisition opens four new markets.
                      The license lists and the intended meaning of “market” are needed.
                      Until then, the states requiring separate authority cannot be
                      identified reliably.

                      - Matter metadata gives a target date of `2026-09-11`. The reported
                      close is “Nov 15,” approximately ten weeks after the Sept. 9
                      intake. A saved hypothetical uses November 15, 2026, but that
                      does not establish the actual closing year. The operative close
                      date and year remain unresolved.


                      ## Decision question


                      Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
                      review before the Nov 15 close?


                      ## Issues


                      <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045 -->

                      ### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                      under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s
                      MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition


                      **Current answer**


                      Mosaic should not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses
                      as assets that automatically move to Mosaic through the reported
                      asset purchase. Mosaic should not start regulated services in
                      a state unless it has documented authority for its complete
                      post-close activity.


                      The acquisition close and the service launch can be managed
                      as separate milestones. If authority is not established, the
                      present fallback is to hold the affected state launch or restrict
                      regulated functions.


                      **Rule and support**


                      Saved research concludes that the answer must be determined
                      state by state. The review must cover Mosaic’s authority, transaction
                      notices or approvals, interim operations, outstanding customer
                      obligations, and Harbor’s license surrender.


                      Four sources were retrieved, but no operative passage was selected,
                      read, or verified. They do not establish the rule in any affected
                      state:


                      - [Money transmission research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)

                      - [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538]

                      - [source:SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4]

                      - [source:SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413]

                      - [source:SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200]


                      The model act is not proof of any state’s adopted law. The premise
                      that an asset purchase does not automatically give Mosaic Harbor’s
                      operating authority remains an unverified state-law conclusion.


                      **Application**


                      Mosaic plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in the new markets.
                      The planned unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access
                      to Mosaic products indicate that Mosaic may become the actual
                      provider. If so, keeping Harbor’s entity or licenses active
                      might not authorize Mosaic’s conduct.


                      Harbor could remain the licensed provider during a transition
                      only if customer contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses,
                      bonds, records, and applicable state rules support that result.
                      The documents and actual operations must match.


                      A partner bank holding funds would not alone resolve the issue.
                      The analysis still depends on who contracts with users, controls
                      transfers, owes repayment, records balances, resolves errors,
                      and performs regulated duties.


                      **Next step**


                      Identify the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare a state matrix.
                      For each state, determine Mosaic’s authority, required filings
                      or approvals, operation while an application is pending, treatment
                      of customer obligations, Harbor’s run-off duties, and the launch
                      restriction needed if authority is not established.

                      The answer must be determined state by state and must cover
                      more than technical change-of-control rules.


                      This path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider
                      and the relevant states permit the arrangement. The unified
                      Mosaic account design may conflict with that position.


                      T'

              title: facts.md
              support_state: supplied
              source_type: workspace
              available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


                - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                Harbor.

                - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.

                - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC''d.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay''s engine on day 1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
                buys Harbor''s assets)

                - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC;
                compliance must confirm.

                - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
                been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR
                history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                ## Assumptions


                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
                acquisition without new state approval

                - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                documents

                - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                in 41 states (per the request).

                - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations
                transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                '

            title: 'Research this issue for the dossier: SAR and alert handling'
            question: 'Research this issue for the dossier: SAR and alert handling:
              obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and
              SARs, and successor liability. About 40 alerts and a handful of prior
              suspicious activity reports remain unreviewed. Delay can affect reporting,
              account treatment, diligence findings, and responsibility between the
              parties.

              Lawyer''s accepted priorities (private matter context):

              Make KYC, alert resolution, and monitoring continuity formal close and
              migration gates.: These linked controls affect the full migrated population
              and can create immediate exposure that is difficult to repair later.

                  text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need

                    text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection
                      5.01 License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the
                      business of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold
                      itself out as providing money transmission unless the person
                      is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does
                      not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate
                      of a person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope
                      of authority conferred by a written contract with the \nlicensee;
                      or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01]
                      and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope
                      of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05]
                      is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent
                      State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between
                      [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized
                      and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions
                      of this [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states
                      that have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes;
                      \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing
                      cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators provided
                      that such protocols are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b)
                      \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner]
                      is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or
                      contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to
                      enable the [Commissioner] to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records;
                      \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing processes and supervision
                      processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication
                      between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to
                      this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
                      to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance
                      with this [Act], including but not limited to, license applications,
                      \napplications for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting,
                      criminal history background\n"

                    text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The
                      renewal report must state or contain a \ndescription of each
                      material change in information submitted by the licensee in
                      its original license \napplication which has not been reported
                      to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause
                      may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner]
                      is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license
                      renewals provided that such functionality is consistent with
                      this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License.
                      \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications
                      or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for
                      a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend
                      or revoke the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures
                      established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for
                      such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money
                      transmission license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will
                      meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all times meet,
                      the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of
                      this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change
                      of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a)
                      \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
                      to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written
                      approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn
                      individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and
                      is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions
                      when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary
                      course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons
                      acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee
                      shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application
                      in a form and in a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner];
                      and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with the request
                      for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may permit
                      a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
                      to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner]
                      pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe
                      application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information
                      \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that
                      have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section
                      5.04] for a licensee.\n"

                    path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
                    text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
                      under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items
                      and address all of the matters that are required, the application
                      shall \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner] shall
                      promptly notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which
                      the application was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1)
                      \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within
                      60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application
                      is not approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion
                      date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person,
                      or group of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited
                      from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good
                      cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination
                      by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis
                      accepted for processing means only that the application, on
                      its face, appears to include all of the \nitems and address
                      all of the matters that are required, and is not an assessment
                      of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
                      of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is
                      filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the
                      [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition and
                      responsibility, financial \nand business experience, character,
                      and general fitness of the person, or group of persons acting
                      in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The [Commissioner]
                      shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this [Section
                      6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following
                      conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of
                      subsections (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and
                      \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility, financial
                      and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general
                      fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert,
                      seeking to acquire control; and the competence, experience,
                      character, \nand general fitness of the key individuals and
                      persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee after the
                      acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of
                      the public to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting
                      in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant
                      avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate licensing
                      \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the
                      process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and
                      when states consider them to have been complete. The intent
                      of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the
                      day an application is determined to be complete.\n"
                  - &id133

                    end: 2523
                    page_number: 23
                    section_label: null
                    body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
                    path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
                    text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized
                      and encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead
                      investigative state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if
                      the \nlead investigative state has sufficient staffing, expertise,
                      and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative
                      state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to
                      investigate the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and
                      \nthe timeframes established by agreement through the multistate
                      licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a
                      formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication to acquire
                      control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny the
                      application. The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice
                      of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
                      An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner]
                      under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30)
                      days16 after receipt of the written notice of the denial \n[pursuant
                      to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements
                      of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing:
                      \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of
                      voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the shareholders or holders
                      of voting shares or voting interests of a \nlicensee or a person
                      in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires control
                      of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires
                      control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian,
                      guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed
                      by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law;
                      \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5)
                      \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject
                      to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA
                      public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control
                      of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a
                      person in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person
                      in control of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons
                      in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation
                      with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15]
                      days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary:
                      Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision
                      may be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a
                      case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative
                      process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating
                      the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

                    body_hash: 4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680
                    path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md
                    text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1)
                      \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply
                      to a \nperson that has complied with and received approval to
                      engage in money transmission \nunder this [Act] or was identified
                      as a person in control in a prior application filed with and
                      \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state
                      pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided that:
                      \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended
                      or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or
                      suspended while the person \nwas in control of the licensee
                      in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee,
                      the person is well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory
                      rating for compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an
                      MSB accredited state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee
                      to be acquired is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections
                      10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition
                      \nof control is completed, and if the person acquiring control
                      is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the
                      requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this
                      [Act] after the acquisition of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe
                      licensee to be acquired will not implement any material \nchanges
                      to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control,
                      and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee
                      also will not implement any material \nchanges to its business
                      plan as a result of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe
                      person provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith
                      the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C),
                      and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner].
                      \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after
                      the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete,
                      the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application
                      for approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson may
                      request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner] as
                      to whether the person \nwould be considered a person in control
                      of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction.
                      If the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be
                      a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and
                      transaction is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a)
                      and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process
                      includes a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and
                      an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate
                      licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
                      and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead
                      investigative state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and
                      \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"
